body:
The simulated cluster runs the real Joulie components on emulated bare-metal nodes, on one machine with Docker. The agent discovers and caps emulated hardware through the same files and tools it uses on a real node, the controller manager reads node power from the simulator’s OpenTelemetry metrics in Prometheus, and the scheduler extender scores real pods. The scripts in scripts/simcluster drive it, and tests/simcluster checks it end to end.
Use it to see a change to the agent, the controller manager, the extender, the chart or the simulator work across components. A change to discovery or capping alone is checked faster by the hwemu tests in cmd/agent (go test ./cmd/agent/ -run Hwemu).
Architecture host: Docker container $SIMCLUSTER_NAME (--privileged): one k3s server Node <name>-infra: the only real kubelet (joulie.io/infra=true, joulie.io/hwemu-host=true) monitoring Prometheus with its OTLP receiver; the Collector in modes otel-collector and otel-bridge joulie-sim the simulator in emulate mode: trees in /var/lib/joulie-hwemu/<node>/, their sys and state served through FUSE at /var/lib/joulie-hwemu/fuse/<node>/ joulie-system the controller manager; the scheduler extender, on the host network or behind its Service joulie-system joulie-agent-emu-<i>: one agent per eligible fake Node, mounting its tree KWOK keeps the fake Nodes Ready fake Nodes rendered from the cluster spec One k3s server in Docker. The container $SIMCLUSTER_NAME (default joulie-sim) runs the k3s image pinned in scripts/simcluster/versions.env. Its own kubelet is the only real Node, <name>-infra, and runs every pod that really runs. The k3s state and the hwemu trees live in the named volumes <name>-k3s and <name>-hwemu, so they outlive a restart of the container: the trees, the limits agents wrote and the energy ledgers that keep exported counters from going back. The trees need no tmpfs: 200 emulated nodes take about 0.1 s per tick on the volume, depending on the machine (Tick cost). Fake Nodes. clusterspec render-nodes turns the cluster spec into Node objects with the labels, taints, capacity and architecture of their hardware profiles, and KWOK v0.8.0 keeps them Ready. Its controller image is pinned by digest (KWOK_IMAGE and KWOK_DIGEST in versions.env) and imported like Prometheus, so the cluster never pulls it. Every fake Node carries sim.joulie.io/cluster=<spec> and sim.joulie.io/pool=<pool>. Emulated hardware. The simulator runs in emulate mode with the same spec: one tree per fake Node under /var/lib/joulie-hwemu on the infra Node, all stepped on one tick. SIMCLUSTER_HWEMU sets how the agents reach the files: fuse, the default, through the simulator’s FUSE views, where a refused write fails at once and counters move at read time; files, the trees themselves. In fuse the k3s container gets /dev/fuse, up.sh makes the hwemu root a shared mount in it, and deploy.sh adds values/simcluster-simulator-fuse.yaml and values/simcluster-fuse.yaml. Emulated agents. The agent binary is the one a release ships, unmodified. With agent.mode: emulated the chart renders one Deployment joulie-agent-emu-<i> per entry of agent.emulated.nodes, on the infra Node, mounting its Node’s tree where the agent reads /sys, /proc/cpuinfo and the GPU tools (Agent chart values). Which Nodes get one is decided as in a real install: simcluster agents renders the chart’s agent DaemonSet with the same values files as the install and keeps the Nodes it would reach. The node selector must match, every NoSchedule and NoExecute taint must be tolerated (counting the tolerations the DaemonSet controller adds), and the architecture must match the image. Every other Node is printed with its reason. Scheduler. SIMCLUSTER_EXTENDER sets how the k3s scheduler reaches the extender. hostnet, the default: the extender runs on the infra Node’s host network and the scheduler calls 127.0.0.1 (scripts/simcluster/manifests/scheduler-config.yaml, the same file the Dagger integration job uses). service: the extender runs off the host network, as a real install defaults to, and the scheduler calls its Service at a fixed ClusterIP (scheduler-config-service.yaml and values/simcluster-extender-service.yaml). Telemetry. The simulator pushes OTLP straight into Prometheus, and the controller manager reads node power and the facility from there with its default settings, or with the settings of the chosen telemetry mode. Access. Every cluster HTTP call goes through the API server’s service proxy. The only published port is the API server’s, on 127.0.0.1, at a port Docker picks. The kubeconfig is $SIMCLUSTER_DIR/kubeconfig; ~/.kube is never read or written. Images. One go build (linux/amd64, CGO off) builds the agent, controller manager, extender, simulator and fakesmi from the working tree. Each binary is wrapped in the distroless image its release uses, tagged joulie.local/joulie-<component>:dev-<first 12 hex of the binary's sha256> (for the simulator image, which also carries fakesmi, a hash of both binaries) and imported into the cluster’s containerd. The images build in parallel, but the imports take turns, one at a time per cluster and only after k3s has imported its air-gap bundle, and a failed import is tried again, three times in all, while the container runs. Pods pull with IfNotPresent, and the deploy checks each pod’s image ID against images.env. Requirements Host. amd64 Linux with Docker allowed to run a --privileged container: k3s runs its kubelet and containerd inside it. The images are built for linux/amd64 only. FUSE. /dev/fuse on the host for SIMCLUSTER_HWEMU=fuse, the default; up.sh refuses to start without it. SIMCLUSTER_HWEMU=files needs none. Tools. docker, kubectl, helm, jq, sha256sum and Go. The scripts build with the toolchain go.mod names (they set GOTOOLCHAIN), so the images match what CI builds. CI installs the Helm release that HELM_VERSION in versions.env pins. k3s 1.34 on a cgroup v1 host. stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup prints tmpfs on cgroup v1. k3s 1.35 and later refuse cgroup v1 unless the kubelet runs with fail-cgroupv1=false; up.sh adds that flag on such a host for such a k3s, but only the pinned 1.34 is tested there. fs.inotify.max_user_instances. Every pod of the cluster runs on the one infra kubelet, so all their containers and file watches share the host’s per-user inotify limit with the host’s own programs. 128 is a common default. The smoke spec fits in it, but a scale run with many emulated agents, or several clusters on one host, may exhaust it. A k3s that gets no instance exits as it starts; the scripts then stop at once with the container’s exit status and log, and name the limit. The scripts never change host settings: check it with sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_instances and raise it by hand before a large run. Pod capacity. Every emulated agent is a pod on the infra Node. up.sh sizes its kubelet for the agents plus 50, at least 110 pods: up to 250 pods with the default /24 per Node, up to 1000 with a /22 per Node and the cluster CIDR 10.64.0.0/12. Beyond 1000 it fails with “split across k3s agents”. A running container created for fewer pods is never resized: up.sh asks for a recreate. Network on the first run. The k3s system images, KWOK, Prometheus, the Collector and the distroless base are pulled once; third-party images are pulled by the digest versions.env pins. With SIMCLUSTER_AIRGAP=1 the k3s system images come from the release’s air-gap bundle, kept in $SIMCLUSTER_DIR/images for later runs. Quick start make simcluster-smoke SIMCLUSTER_KEEP=1 D=~/.cache/joulie/simcluster/joulie-sim-smoke jq '{status: ."test.suite.run.status", failures}' $D/runs/latest/summary.json export KUBECONFIG=$D/kubeconfig kubectl get nodes -L sim.joulie.io/pool kubectl get nodetwins -o custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,SRC:.status.powerMeasurement.source,W:.status.powerMeasurement.measuredNodePowerW make simcluster-down SIMCLUSTER_NAME=joulie-sim-smoke make simcluster-smoke creates the cluster joulie-sim-smoke from tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml, deploys with tests/simcluster/smoke-values.yaml, runs TestSimclusterE2E, collects the results and deletes the cluster unless SIMCLUSTER_KEEP=1. It builds the images and compiles the test while the cluster starts. The test times out after ten rate windows of the timing, at least 20 minutes, unless SIMCLUSTER_TEST_TIMEOUT sets another. The smoke spec has nine Nodes: an Intel Xeon with RAPL, an AMD EPYC with energy counters only, an AMD EPYC with HSMP, an H100 NVL node, an H100 SXM node with persistence mode off, an MI300X node, a virtual machine, a managed Intel node with a taint of its own, which the agent tolerates, and a managed arm64 node, which no agent reaches because the images are built for amd64 only. The smoke values put every node in performance with CPU and GPU caps at 80 %; the test lowers them to 50 % halfway.
To keep a cluster and work on it step by step:
make simcluster-up # k3s, KWOK, Prometheus, the fake Nodes make simcluster-deploy # images, simulator, Joulie; waits until every component reports make simcluster-status Targets Each target runs one script of scripts/simcluster and nothing else, so make -n shows what will run. The scripts also run directly, and each starts with its usage.
Target Script What it does simcluster-up up.sh Validates the spec (simcluster validate). Creates the k3s container, or reuses an existing one, starting it when stopped, if it was created for at least as many pods and as large pod CIDRs, with the same scheduler configuration (SIMCLUSTER_EXTENDER) and k3s image; otherwise it says to recreate. Installs KWOK, Prometheus and, in modes otel-collector and otel-bridge, the Collector. Applies the spec’s Nodes and deletes the fake Nodes the spec no longer names. simcluster-images images.sh Builds and imports the Joulie images, and the pinned third-party ones, and writes images.env. An unchanged binary keeps its tag and is not imported again. Run directly, --wait-container builds first and then waits for the cluster’s container to run, so the build overlaps the cluster’s start. simcluster-deploy deploy.sh Images, CRDs, the simulator, the agent placement, Joulie. Waits for the rollouts (polling one list of the namespace’s workloads, for 5 minutes plus 5 seconds per workload; on a timeout it prints what did not roll out and the pods that are not ready), one NodeHardware per emulated agent, the series of every measured Node and a NodeTwin per managed Node, then checks every pod’s image. -f <values> adds a Joulie values file when run directly. simcluster-reload C=<component> reload.sh Rebuilds and rolls out agent, controller-manager, scheduler, simulator or all; see the dev loop. simcluster-status status.sh Prints every Node with its pool, profile and NodeTwin power. Exits 1 when a Node is NotReady, a pod without joulie.io/workload-class is bound to a fake Node, a pod runs another image than images.env names, an emulated agent’s Node has no NodeHardware, or a measured Node has no series. simcluster-tree [NODE=<node>] tree.sh Without a Node, lists the Nodes that have a tree; with one, prints every file of its tree with its first line: the energy counters, limits, frequencies and GPU state its agent sees. simcluster-logs C=<component> [NODE=<node>] logs.sh The last 200 lines of agent (one Node’s, or every agent’s), controller-manager, scheduler, simulator, prometheus, otelcol, kwok or k3s. Run directly, it passes further flags such as -f to kubectl logs. simcluster-smoke smoke.sh See Quick start. simcluster-down down.sh Removes the container with its anonymous volumes and the named volumes <name>-k3s and <name>-hwemu. Keeps images/, runs/ and bin/ of the state directory. Settings The scripts read these variables from the environment; make passes on the ones that are set.
Variable Default Effect SIMCLUSTER_NAME joulie-sim; joulie-sim-smoke for the smoke run Container name and prefix of its volumes. It must match ^joulie-sim(-[a-z0-9]+)*$: the scripts touch no container or volume named otherwise. SIMCLUSTER_DIR ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/joulie/simcluster/<name> State directory, outside the repository (below). SIMCLUSTER_SPEC tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml The cluster spec. tests/simcluster/specs/medium.yaml has 50 Nodes, 48 of them reached by the agent, with GPU sharing, AMD GPUs with a pinned power cap, Nodes without NFD labels or GPU driver tools, and an unmanaged pool. tests/simcluster/specs/profiles.yaml has one Node of every builtin profile. tests/simcluster/specs/demo.yaml has 10 Nodes in five hardware families, the cluster of the kubectl joulie recording (scripts/kubectl-joulie-demo.sh). SIMCLUSTER_NODES (empty) Instead of a spec, this many Nodes of one profile, for scale runs. SIMCLUSTER_SCALE_PROFILE intel-xeon-2s-rapl The profile of SIMCLUSTER_NODES. SIMCLUSTER_TELEMETRY otel The telemetry mode. SIMCLUSTER_POWER_SCOPE components The node power scope Joulie reads: components (CPU packages and GPUs) or host (hw.host.*, in every otel mode but otel-bridge). SIMCLUSTER_TIMING dev The timing profile, a file scripts/simcluster/timing/<name>.env. SIMCLUSTER_HWEMU fuse How the emulated agents reach their Node’s files: fuse (the simulator’s FUSE views of sys and state, mounted with propagation HostToContainer) or files (the trees’ own files). deploy.sh records it in deploy.env, so a reload keeps it. SIMCLUSTER_EXTENDER hostnet How the k3s scheduler reaches the extender: hostnet (the extender on the infra Node’s host network, at 127.0.0.1) or service (the extender off the host network, through its Service). The container is created for one of them; up.sh asks for a recreate to switch. SIMCLUSTER_PROFILES_DIR (empty) Local hardware profiles, read by the host tools only: the scripts always pass it as their -profiles-dir, so SIM_PROFILES_DIR does not apply. The simulator in the cluster reads its builtin profiles, so up.sh refuses a spec that needs a local one. SIMCLUSTER_EXTRA_VALUES (empty) Joulie values files, space separated, installed after values/simcluster.yaml and the generated files. They also decide which Nodes get an emulated agent. SIMCLUSTER_SIM_EXTRA_VALUES (empty) Simulator values files, space separated, installed after values/simcluster-simulator.yaml and the generated file. deploy.sh records them in deploy.env, so a later reload.sh installs with them too. SIMCLUSTER_KEEP 0 1 keeps the smoke cluster after the run. SIMCLUSTER_TEST_TIMEOUT ten RATE_WINDOWs of the timing, at least 20m (20m in dev, 50m in production) Timeout of TestSimclusterE2E in the smoke run, a Go duration. SIMCLUSTER_AIRGAP 0 1 loads the k3s system images from the release’s air-gap bundle. SIMCLUSTER_FORCE_RELOAD 0 1 makes every reload a reload.sh --force. COMPONENT (or C), NODE (empty) The component and the Node of simcluster-reload, simcluster-logs and simcluster-tree. The state directory holds kubeconfig; cluster.env (how the container was created); telemetry.env, spec.yaml, images.env, deploy.env and crds.sha (what is installed); values/ and render/ (generated values files, renders and configurations); bin/ (the binaries, with the host tools in bin/host); images/ (image tarballs); and runs/ (the run results).
Telemetry modes A mode sets how the emulated Nodes’ power reaches Prometheus and which Joulie input settings read it. Every mode is checked against the emulator’s truth, read from the simulator’s /debug/emulate.
SIMCLUSTER_TELEMETRY Path to Prometheus Joulie settings beyond the defaults Checked against otel (default) the simulator pushes OTLP; Prometheus promotes k8s.node.name and host.name none CPU packages plus GPUs otel-unpromoted as otel, without promotion none: auto falls back to joining target_info CPU packages plus GPUs otel-labels-unpromoted as otel-unpromoted PROMETHEUS_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=labels no data, with the promotion hint in the log otel-utf8 as otel, names translated with NoUTF8EscapingWithSuffixes PROMETHEUS_NAME_TRANSLATION=NoUTF8EscapingWithSuffixes CPU packages plus GPUs otel-collector the simulator pushes to an OpenTelemetry Collector, whose prometheus exporter Prometheus scrapes with honor_labels: true none CPU packages plus GPUs otel-bridge the simulator pushes no OTLP and serves kepler-0.12, dcgm-4.8.4 and amd-dme-1.5.2; a contrib Collector runs examples/11-otel-collector-bridge/collector.yaml against them and pushes hw.* to Prometheus, the CPU as power gauges none; the facility metrics stay off, as the chart has them CPU packages plus GPUs, with the queries of Joulie’s otel preset kepler the simulator also serves Kepler 0.12 series, GPUs included (SIM_KEPLER012_GPU=true) NODE_POWER_PRESET=kepler CPU packages plus NVIDIA GPUs kepler-legacy the simulator also serves Kepler 0.7 series, scraped with honor_labels: false NODE_POWER_PRESET=kepler-legacy CPU packages plus NVIDIA GPUs With SIMCLUSTER_POWER_SCOPE=host, an otel mode other than otel-bridge, which carries no whole-host power, also sets NODE_POWER_SCOPE=host and is checked against whole-host power. Each check passes within 3 % of the truth, and never needs to be closer than 1 W. simcluster telemetry prints what a mode generates, for example go run ./simulator/cmd/simcluster telemetry --part prom-config --mode otel-utf8; the parts are prom-config, otelcol-config, sim-values, joulie-values, checks and wait.
Timing Timing names map onto the real settings, so a nightly run in production timing exercises the values a real install uses.
Timing setting dev production Becomes CONTROLLER_RECONCILE_INTERVAL 10s 1m controller manager RECONCILE_INTERVAL AGENT_RECONCILE_INTERVAL 5s 20s agent RECONCILE_INTERVAL AGENT_SPEC_READ_TIMEOUT 60s 5m agent SPEC_READ_TIMEOUT PROM_SCRAPE_INTERVAL 5s 1m Prometheus scrape_interval OTLP_EXPORT_INTERVAL_MS 5000 60000 simulator otel.exportIntervalMillis RATE_WINDOW 30s 5m controller manager PROMETHEUS_RATE_WINDOW FACILITY_POLL_INTERVAL 10s 30s controller manager FACILITY_POLL_INTERVAL A rate window shorter than four export intervals reads too few samples.
What a real Prometheus needs The harness configures its Prometheus the way a production one must be configured for Joulie’s OpenTelemetry inputs: --web.enable-otlp-receiver, k8s.node.name and host.name promoted onto the series, the translation strategy Joulie expects, and an out-of-order window for samples that carry the producer’s timestamps. The settings, the kube-prometheus-stack values (values/prometheus-grafana.yaml) and the pitfalls are under Prometheus settings and Pitfalls. The modes otel-unpromoted, otel-labels-unpromoted and otel-utf8 check what Joulie reads when the promotion is missing or the strategy differs.
The dev loop make simcluster-up && make simcluster-deploy # once # edit the agent make simcluster-reload C=agent # rebuild, import, roll out; prints the seconds make simcluster-logs C=agent NODE=intel-0 make simcluster-tree NODE=intel-0 make simcluster-status A reload follows the binary, not the sources. The image tag is the binary’s sha256, so reload.sh imports and upgrades only when the binary changed; an unchanged binary changes nothing, with no import, no upgrade and no restart. Touching a source file is therefore a no-op. To restart a component anyway, use reload.sh <component> --force (through make, SIMCLUSTER_FORCE_RELOAD=1), which sets the pod template annotation sim.joulie.io/reload to the current time. A reload rolls out one component. The others keep their images and pods even when shared code changed their binaries too; reload them, or all. A reload re-reads the charts and values files, reruns the release’s helm upgrade with only the component’s tag changed, and re-applies the CRDs when they changed. The values files are those of the last deploy, as deploy.env records them, a scenario’s simulator.set (SIMCLUSTER_SIM_EXTRA_VALUES) included. Another spec or mode. up.sh with another SIMCLUSTER_SPEC applies its Nodes and deletes the ones it no longer names; deploy.sh sets Prometheus up again when the mode or the timing changed. Reading Prometheus and the truth, through the API server proxy: export KUBECONFIG=~/.cache/joulie/simcluster/joulie-sim/kubeconfig P=/api/v1/namespaces/monitoring/services/prometheus-operated:9090/proxy/api/v1/query pq() { kubectl get --raw "$P?query=$(jq -rn --arg q "$1" '$q|@uri')" | jq -c '[.data.result[] | [.metric.k8s_node_name, .value[1]]]'; } pq 'sum by (k8s_node_name) (rate(hw_host_energy_joules_total[30s]))' kubectl get --raw /api/v1/namespaces/joulie-sim/services/joulie-telemetry-sim:80/proxy/debug/emulate | jq '[.nodes[] | {name, hostW: .host.powerW}]' Deviations from a real cluster KWOK taint. Every fake Node carries the KWOK annotation and the taint kwok.x-k8s.io/node=fake:NoSchedule, which keeps infrastructure pods off it. A pod meant for a fake Node must tolerate it. Placement ignores this taint, since a real Node does not have it. The sim.joulie.io/cluster selector. The infra Node runs a real kubelet, so a workload pod could land there. The simulator’s workload pods select sim.joulie.io/cluster=<spec> by default, and nothing without joulie.io/workload-class may be bound to a fake Node (status.sh checks it). Agents are Deployments, unprivileged. On a real node the agent is a DaemonSet pod with host network and privileges. An emulated agent is a Deployment on the infra Node with privileged: false and no host network, and its NODE_NAME is a literal. A privileged pod would see the infra host’s real devices on every fake Node, and only one host-network agent fits on a Node. /dev/nvidiactl is a file. On NVIDIA Nodes the tree has an empty regular file mounted at /dev/nvidiactl, where a privileged agent on a real node sees the driver’s character device. The agent only checks that it exists. Tool stubs. nvidia-smi, rocm-smi and amd-smi are links to fakesmi, first on the agent’s PATH. fakesmi checks what the real tool needs before it runs (the ELF loader, the C libraries and NVML for nvidia-smi, a script’s interpreter; see Simulator hardware emulation). A pool’s toolDelivery under spec.harness.pools sets what they find. mounted: the harness mounts one stub file at the first path of each requirement (seven on an NVIDIA Node, two on an AMD one), standing in for a node where the chart’s hooks deliver the driver; the stub is never run. none: nothing, so the tools fail as on a node without driver tools. A pool that does not set it follows the Joulie install: mounted only with agent.runtimeClassName or agent.extraVolumes, otherwise none, as a default install has it. The specs in tests/simcluster/specs/ set it on every GPU pool. Only a profile whose tools list requirements can fail this way: a tool without requirements always runs. With SIMCLUSTER_HWEMU=files, writes and counters move once per tick. A write the driver would refuse, such as one to a RAPL limit the firmware locks, succeeds and reads back until the next tick, which reverts it and reports joulie.sim.write.rejected with the errno a real kernel returns at once as error.type (enodata for a locked RAPL limit, einval, ebusy and so on; see Events). The writes made between two ticks are applied in order of modification time, and two writes to one file count as the last. energy_uj changes once per SIM_EMULATE_TICK, so a reader that turns energy differences into power over its own wall-clock interval is off by up to tick / interval per reading (20 % at a 1 s tick and a 5 s interval), without accumulating. The default, fuse, has none of these. A simulator restart in FUSE mode. Until the new simulator serves its views, seconds after its pod starts, the agents’ reads of /host-sys and /emu/state fail with ENOTCONN; they recover without a restart (check E17). Each restart leaves the old views mounted underneath until make simcluster-down. A root with directory limits is not resumed. A tree in which locked limits are directories, as an older simulator rendered them, stops the start with ErrTreeConflict. Remove the root (make simcluster-down removes the volume <name>-hwemu) and deploy again. Fake Nodes have no kubelet. KWOK moves a pod bound to a fake Node through its phases (its stages, plus scripts/simcluster/manifests/stage-*.yaml); no container runs, and the Node’s power is the simulator’s model of its load. Checks make simcluster-smoke runs TestSimclusterE2E (tests/simcluster, build tag simcluster) against the deployed cluster. Each check is one entry under assertions in the run’s summary.json, with its status, observed and expected values. The list of checks, and what each one asserts, is in tests/simcluster/README.md. The test changes the cluster as it goes (the caps go to 50 %, the extender is reloaded), so it expects a fresh deploy.
Run results Each smoke run writes $SIMCLUSTER_DIR/runs/<UTC>-<spec>-<mode>-<sha12>[-dirty]/, and runs/latest points at the newest. down.sh keeps them.
summary.json, schema joulie.simcluster.summary/v1: test.suite.name, test.suite.run.status (success, failure, timed_out or aborted), exitCode, failures, warnings, knownDefects (see the tests README), one entry per check under assertions (test.case.name, test.case.result.status, observed and expected), the spec, mode, scope and timing, the git commit and whether the tree was dirty, the images, and the semantic conventions schema URL. otlp/harness.metrics.jsonl and otlp/harness.logs.jsonl: one OTLP JSON object per line, with a joulie.scenario.assertion.evaluated log record and joulie.scenario.assertion.value points per check. k8s/ (the Nodes, NodeHardware, NodeTwins, pods and events at the end), logs/ (every pod in joulie-system, joulie-sim and monitoring, k3s’s whole log as k3s.log and containerd’s as containerd.log, also from a container that exited), values.effective.yaml and values.simulator.effective.yaml, images.env, deploy.env, cluster.env, and smoke.log, everything the run printed. The scenario runner writes the same layout and schema, so one reader serves both.

title: Simulated Cluster

body:
A workload scenario runs a workload through the simulated cluster and checks what happened: whether the jobs completed, where they were placed, how long they took, what energy they used, and how Joulie’s settings compare with each other or with no Joulie at all. The jobs are real Kubernetes Jobs, scheduled by the real scheduler and the Joulie extender onto KWOK Nodes, and the simulator’s v1 workload engine drives them on the emulated hardware, so a cap the agent writes slows the jobs on that Node.
A scenario is one file in tests/simcluster/scenarios/. scripts/simcluster/scenario.sh runs it and simscenario (simulator/cmd/simscenario) validates, plans and evaluates it.
Quick start make simcluster-scenario SCENARIO=tests/simcluster/scenarios/smoke.yaml jq '{status: ."test.suite.run.status", failures, jobs}' ~/.cache/joulie/simcluster/joulie-sim/runs/latest/summary.json make simcluster-down The first command creates the cluster (or reuses a running one), deploys the simulator and Joulie built from the working tree, runs the scenario’s jobs and evaluates them. It exits 0 when every assertion of severity fail passed, 1 when one failed, and 2 when the scenario is invalid or a variant could not be run. The cluster is kept, so a second scenario on the same spec starts in seconds; make simcluster-down deletes it.
To check a scenario without a cluster:
go run ./simulator/cmd/simscenario validate tests/simcluster/scenarios/nightly-mixed.yaml go build -o /tmp/bin/ ./simulator/cmd/workloadgen go run ./simulator/cmd/simscenario plan tests/simcluster/scenarios/nightly-mixed.yaml -out /tmp/plan -workloadgen /tmp/bin/workloadgen plan writes the trace and prints, for each resource, the offered load (the sum over the jobs due in the window of request times ideal runtime, over capacity times the window) and when the work can end at the earliest: the latest, over the due times T, of T plus the runtime of a job due then and of T plus the work due from T on over the capacity, against the deadline (duration plus drain). It refuses a load above 0.9, which would queue jobs past any drain, and an earliest end past 0.9 of the deadline, which a burst of late arrivals or a long last job causes at any load. For a variant on static_partition (the controller manager’s default policy, read from joulie.set with its STATIC_HP_FRAC and NODE_SELECTOR), performance pods run only on the Nodes the policy keeps in performance (policy.BuildStaticPlan over the spec’s Nodes), so plan checks the performance jobs against those Nodes too and prints that table separately. A variant without Joulie, or on queue_aware_v1, which grows its performance set with the demand, is checked on every Node.
The library Scenario Cluster spec, timing Workload Checks smoke smoke, dev; about 7 minutes 9 inline jobs: CPU and GPU, both classes, NVIDIA and AMD every job completes through KWOK; no stall; no Job left incomplete and no stray pod on a fake Node; 9 joulie.sim.job.completed events; energy above 0 J perf-isolation policy, dev performance and standard CPU jobs, and one standard job pinned to the eco Node intel-2 no performance pod is bound to a Node that was eco for longer than the placement grace; standard jobs completed on an eco Node and intel-2 drew CPU energy, so the check is not vacuous cap-cost policy, dev CPU jobs that nearly fill an intel Node; GPU jobs with no CPU feed cpu-cap-cost: the median slowdown of CPU jobs on the eco Node exceeds that on performance Nodes by more than 5 %; gpu-unaffected-by-cpu-cap: the median slowdown of the GPU jobs stays within 2 % deadlock-visible smoke, dev one gang of 2 pods of 8 GPUs, both pinned to nvl-0, which has 8 the run reports joulie.sim.run.stalled and a gang_incomplete stall, and the gang never completes demo demo, dev; 40 minutes of arrivals, 10 to drain 112 inline jobs on 10 Nodes in five hardware families: NVIDIA training and inference, AMD fine-tuning, performance and standard CPU jobs, half the Nodes in eco; the cluster of the kubectl joulie recording, scripts/kubectl-joulie-demo.sh no performance pod is bound to an eco Node; at least 90 % of the jobs complete nightly-mixed nightly, production; a 60 minute run, 20 to drain workloadgen seed 7: arrivals at a constant rate over 55 minutes, jobs of at most 15 minutes; offered load 0.3 to 0.8 of the CPUs and both GPU kinds, of the cluster and, for the performance jobs, of the performance Nodes at least 95 % of the due jobs complete; no performance pod on eco; no run stall; the NodeTwins’ measured power within 15 % of the emulated energy rate at p95 (warning) weekly-compare nightly, production the nightly workload, three variants on fresh clusters: joulie-off, queue-aware, kepler-compat per variant as nightly; Joulie spends no more energy than joulie-off, and its performance jobs take at most 10 % longer at p95 (warnings) cap-cost sets GPU_ECO_CAP_PCT_OF_MAX=100, so every GPU is uncapped and the eco CPU cap is the only cap in play. The controller manager gives the CPU of a GPU Node the performance cap whatever its profile, and a GPU job whose CPU feed intensity is 0 would not feel a CPU cap anyway, so gpu-unaffected-by-cpu-cap checks that the CPU cap costs such a job nothing. No GPU cap is measured. perf-isolation and cap-cost pin static_partition with STATIC_HP_FRAC=0.5, which on the policy spec puts intel-2, epyc-1 and nvl-1 in eco.
The specs the library adds, in tests/simcluster/specs/, carry no baseLoad, so a Node idles until a run’s jobs load it:
policy.yaml: 3 intel-xeon-2s-rapl, 2 amd-epyc-2s-energy-only, 2 nvidia-h100-nvl-8gpu. Every family has more than one Node, so the policy keeps an eco Node in each. nightly.yaml: 16 intel-xeon-2s-rapl, 12 amd-epyc-2s-energy-only, 4 amd-epyc-2s-hsmp, 8 nvidia-h100-nvl-8gpu, 4 nvidia-h100-sxm-8gpu, 4 amd-instinct-mi300x-8gpu, 2 vm-no-powercap. How a run works scenario.sh <file>:
builds simscenario and workloadgen, validates the scenario and plans the run directory: scenario.effective.yaml (the scenario with its defaults filled in) and, per variant, trace.jsonl and variant.env; per variant: deletes the cluster first when the scenario isolates its variants (it lists more than one, or sets isolation: cluster), then runs up.sh, which creates the cluster or reuses a running one and switches it to the variant’s spec; runs deploy.sh with the variant’s spec, timing, telemetry mode and Joulie values files. joulie.set and simulator.set become values files, rendered by helm from the --set arguments so they mean exactly what --set means; with joulie.enabled: false, uninstalls Joulie, deletes its NodeTwins and NodeHardwares, removes the joulie.io/power-profile labels and, once no Joulie pod is left, renders the Nodes’ hwemu trees again: an agent writes its limits into the tree and never restores them, so without this the variant would run under the caps the agents wrote during the deploy; deletes and creates the run’s namespaces, and copies the trace into the simulator’s run directory, <SIM_HWEMU_ROOT>/_runs/<run id>/trace.jsonl, with docker exec; simscenario run: checks the KWOK pod-complete Stage, snapshots the Nodes and Joulie’s objects, starts the run through the simulator’s run API, captures the NodeTwins every capture interval until the run finishes, its deadline (duration plus drain) passes or it stays stalled for abortOnRunStalled, snapshots again, finishes the run (deleting its Job objects), records the Prometheus captures and collects the component logs. Everything goes through the API server, nothing is port-forwarded; copies the simulator’s otlp/ files out of the cluster, and simscenario evaluate writes the variant’s summary.json; simscenario summarize writes the run’s summary.json with the comparisons across variants, and runs/latest points at the run directory. Scenario files A scenario is decoded strictly: an unknown key anywhere, including inside an assertion, is an error. Durations are Go durations such as 90s or 4m.
Key Meaning schemaVersion 1 name the file stem, a DNS label cluster.spec, cluster.timing a cluster spec, relative to the repository root; dev (default) or production seed seeds the plan and workloadgen duration, drain the submission window (at most 6 h; jobs due later are dropped) and the extra time for submitted jobs to finish abortOnRunStalled end the run once joulie.sim.run.stalled has lasted this long isolation cluster (each variant on a fresh cluster, the default with several variants) or reuse (allowed with one variant only) workload the run’s settings and exactly one source: jobs, generate or trace (below) joulie enabled (default true), inputPreset (otel, kepler or kepler-legacy), set (Helm --set pairs) and values (values files) simulator.set Helm --set pairs for the simulator release variants up to 4, each a name, a description and its own joulie and simulator, merged key by key over the top level capture interval of the NodeTwin captures (default 15s) and prometheus range queries recorded as gauges named joulie.capture.* assertions, compare below A scenario may not set NODE_POWER_* or FACILITY_*, neither in joulie.set nor in a values file: it reaches Joulie’s inputs only through joulie.inputPreset, so it always tests a preset Joulie ships.
joulie.set and simulator.set take --set syntax: {a,b} is a list, and a comma inside a value needs a backslash.
The workload workload.namespace, owner, intent, completion, jobTTL, stallReport, baseSpeedPerCore and placement become the run’s options (the SIM_WORKLOAD_* defaults of the configuration reference apply to what is unset). baseSpeedPerCore (default 1) sizes the trace and is sent with the run, so ideal runtimes hold whatever the simulator was deployed with. placement replaces the simulator’s default node selector (sim.joulie.io/cluster=<spec>) and tolerations (the KWOK taint); an empty list or map clears the default, an unset one keeps it.
The sources:
jobs: inline job kinds. Each is name, class (performance or standard), count groups submitted every apart, pods per group (a gang with gang: true), requests (cpu and memory), gpus (resource: nvidia.com/gpu, amd.com/gpu, nvidia.com/gpu.shared or nvidia.com/mig-<profile>, and count), the ideal runtime, workClass, profile (cpuUtilization, gpuUtilization, memoryIntensity, ioIntensity, cpuFeedIntensityGpu, and peerTransferIntensity, the share of a multi-GPU job’s GPU time spent copying between its GPUs, see Peer transfers), sensitivity, and the pod’s affinity, nodeSelector and tolerations. generate.workloadgen: workloadgen flags without the dash, from an allowlist. The runner sets seed, base-speed-per-core, out and schema-version (always v3) itself. trace: a v3 trace file, relative to the repository root. k3s does not run the ExtendedResourceToleration admission plugin, so nothing adds the GPU vendor’s toleration to a pod that requests GPUs. The GPU profiles taint their Nodes (nvidia.com/gpu, amd.com/gpu), so a GPU job needs that toleration in its tolerations, or the run’s placement.tolerations (as the nightly scenarios do, restating the KWOK toleration the list replaces).
Assertions Every assertion has a name, a type and a severity (fail, the default, or warn), and an expect comparator such as ">= 0.95", "== 0", "< 90s" or "> 0 J". An assertion with nothing to evaluate fails with “no data”.
Type Fields Observed jobs a job filter (class, workload, nodeProfile); expect per count: completedFraction, completed, failed, incomplete the jobs due before the duration latency a job filter, metric (duration, queueWait, runTime, slowdown), quantile (0.5 to 1, or max), optional reference filter the quantile over completed jobs, or its ratio to the reference jobs’ quantile stall expect per reason: gangIncomplete, noProgress, runStalled stall events placement class, forbidden schedulable classes, graceSeconds binds of that class to a Node that had held a forbidden class for at least the grace (default the extender’s CACHE_TTL plus the reconcile interval) energy scope (total, class:<class>, node:<node>), hwType (cpu, gpu, all), perJob joulie.sim.workload.energy at the end events event, where attribute values matching log records objects expect per count: jobsNotComplete, strayPodsOnFakeNodes, nodeHardwares, controlBlocked the objects at the end twinPower warmup, tolerance, quantile, nodes the quantile of the relative error between each NodeTwin’s measured power and its Node’s energy rate promql query, at: end one instant query at the end of the run slowdown is run time over ideal run time, so queueing does not count. The nodeProfile of a job is its Node’s power profile when its pod was bound.
Comparisons compare entries take a metric of a variant over the same metric of a reference variant, with an expect on the ratio and a severity. Metrics: energy.total, class.<class>.energy, class.<class>.throughput, and class.<class>.<duration|queueWait|slowdown>.<p50|p95|max>.
Results A run directory, $SIMCLUSTER_DIR/runs/<UTC>-<scenario>-<sha12>[-dirty]/, holds scenario.effective.yaml, scenario.log and a summary.json; each variant writes <variant>/ (a scenario without variants writes these at the top):
summary.json, schema joulie.simcluster.summary/v1, the same as the smoke test’s: test.suite.name, test.suite.run.status, exitCode, failures, warnings, one entry per check under assertions, and for scenarios jobs, classes (throughput, energy, slowdown and duration quantiles per class), energy (boundary cpu packages + gpus) and comparisons; otlp/simulator.metrics.jsonl and otlp/simulator.logs.jsonl, the simulator’s run records, and otlp/harness.metrics.jsonl and otlp/harness.logs.jsonl, the runner’s: OTLP JSON Lines with the names of Simulator Metrics; trace.jsonl, variant.env, run-status.json, values.effective.yaml, values.simulator.effective.yaml, images.env, the snapshots in k8s/ and the component logs in logs/; a variant that could not be run gets the cluster’s k3s.log and containerd.log there instead. With SIMCLUSTER_VALIDATE_OTLP=1, every line of every OTLP file is also posted to an OpenTelemetry Collector (OTELCOL_IMAGE pinned to OTELCOL_DIGEST of scripts/simcluster/versions.env, one container in Docker for the whole scenario, with the OTLP receiver and the file exporter). Each post must answer HTTP 200 with no rejected points or records, and the Collector must write as many data points and log records as were sent; otherwise the variant fails.
Settings scenario.sh reads these besides the settings of up.sh and deploy.sh (Simulated Cluster). Each variant’s variant.env sets the spec, timing, telemetry mode and power scope, and scenario.sh passes a scenario’s simulator.set to deploy.sh through SIMCLUSTER_SIM_EXTRA_VALUES.
Variable Default Effect SCENARIO (none) The scenario file, for make simcluster-scenario SCENARIO_VARIANTS (empty: all) Run only these variants, space separated. The run is then not summarized, so the variants can run on separate machines and simscenario summarize can compare them afterwards SCENARIO_RUN_DIR a new $SIMCLUSTER_DIR/runs/<UTC>-<scenario>-<sha12>[-dirty] The run directory; runs/latest is left alone when it is set SIMCLUSTER_VALIDATE_OTLP (unset) 1 posts the run’s OTLP files to a Collector, above SIMCLUSTER_SCENARIOS (unset) 1 makes make simcluster-smoke also run the smoke scenario on its cluster after the end-to-end test, into the smoke run’s scenario-smoke/ simscenario simscenario validate <file> [-repo DIR] simscenario plan <file> -out RUNDIR [-repo DIR] [-workloadgen BIN] simscenario run -variant-dir DIR [-kubeconfig FILE] simscenario evaluate DIR simscenario summarize RUNDIR Exit codes: 0 success, 1 a failed assertion or comparison of severity fail, 2 a usage error, an invalid scenario, or a run that could not be carried out.
CI CI runs nightly-mixed and deadlock-visible Monday to Saturday and weekly-compare on Sundays; the schedule is in tests/simcluster/README.md.

body:
This page installs the simulator into a Kubernetes cluster you already have, or runs it from a workstation. To try Joulie on emulated nodes with nothing but Docker, use the simulated cluster instead: it creates the cluster and installs everything.
Every command below uses the namespace joulie-sim-demo and the release joulie-simulator, the defaults of make simulator-install.
Prerequisites A Kubernetes cluster (real, or kind for local work), with kubectl pointed at it. helm v3 or later. Install with Helm The simulator chart is published next to the Joulie chart:
helm upgrade --install joulie-simulator oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie-sim \ --version <version> -n joulie-sim-demo --create-namespace helm show values oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie-sim --version <version> prints the values you can override with -f values.yaml. helm uninstall joulie-simulator -n joulie-sim-demo removes it.
The chart sets SIM_NODE_SELECTOR=joulie.io/managed=true, so the simulator models the Nodes with that label. KWOK and Standalone Modes says how to point Joulie at it.
Install from source From the repository root, build and push an image, then install the chart in charts/joulie-simulator with it:
make simulator-build-push TAG=<tag> make simulator-install TAG=<tag> make simulator-install runs helm upgrade --install and waits for the rollout. kubectl apply -f simulator/deploy/simulator.yaml installs the same simulator from plain manifests, with the image latest.
Verify kubectl -n joulie-sim-demo rollout status deploy/joulie-telemetry-sim kubectl -n joulie-sim-demo logs deploy/joulie-telemetry-sim --tail=50 kubectl -n joulie-sim-demo port-forward svc/joulie-telemetry-sim 18080:80 & curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18080/healthz # 200 when healthy curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18080/debug/nodes | jq # the Nodes it models curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18080/metrics | head -30 # its Prometheus metrics The Service is joulie-telemetry-sim on port 80; in the cluster the simulator’s URL is http://joulie-telemetry-sim.joulie-sim-demo.svc.cluster.local. The endpoints are listed under HTTP API.
Emulate mode in a cluster Emulate mode needs a cluster spec and one node that holds the emulated trees. The chart then runs the simulator as root with one replica and strategy Recreate, on the Node labelled joulie.io/hwemu-host=true, with emulate.root as a hostPath:
kubectl label node <node> joulie.io/hwemu-host=true helm upgrade --install joulie-simulator charts/joulie-simulator -n joulie-sim-demo --create-namespace \ --set emulate.enabled=true \ --set-file emulate.clusterSpec=tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml \ --set otel.metricsEndpoint=http://prometheus-operated.monitoring:9090/api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics The pod is Ready once every tree exists, so agent pods that mount the trees (agent.mode: emulated in the Joulie chart, see Agent chart values) can start after it. Apply the spec’s Nodes with clusterspec render-nodes (The cluster spec). The chart values are under Simulator emulate mode.
Emulate mode from a workstation The simulator also runs outside the cluster, against any cluster a kubeconfig reaches, which is the fastest loop while changing it. Use a throwaway cluster: the Nodes it renders are fake and carry the KWOK taint.
export KUBECONFIG=<kubeconfig of a throwaway cluster> go build -o /tmp/sim/bin/ ./simulator/cmd/simulator ./simulator/cmd/clusterspec /tmp/sim/bin/clusterspec render-nodes -spec tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml | kubectl apply -f - SIM_EMULATE=true SIM_CLUSTER_SPEC=tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml \ SIM_HWEMU_ROOT=/tmp/sim/hwemu SIM_FAKESMI_SOURCE= SIM_DEBUG_PERSIST_DIR=/tmp/sim/run \ SIM_EXPORTERS=kepler-0.7,dcgm-4.8.4 \ /tmp/sim/bin/simulator Outside a pod the simulator listens on 127.0.0.1:18080. SIM_FAKESMI_SOURCE= skips the fakesmi install, which only agent pods need. The log names the API server in use. Then:
curl -s 127.0.0.1:18080/debug/emulate | jq -c '[.nodes[] | [.name, .host.powerW]]' curl -s 127.0.0.1:18080/exporters/kepler-0.7/metrics | grep kepler_node_platform_joules_total head -1 /tmp/sim/run/events.jsonl | jq -r '.resourceLogs[0].scopeLogs[0].logRecords[0].eventName' Add OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics to push to a local Prometheus. Stopping and starting the simulator over the same SIM_HWEMU_ROOT resumes the trees.

body:
Emulate mode emulates the bare-metal nodes of a cluster spec at the boundary the agent sees: the files it reads and writes, and the GPU tools it runs. An unmodified agent then runs its real discovery and capping code against each node, while Kubernetes scheduling stays real. The simulated cluster runs it; to run it yourself, see Installation. Nodes the spec does not list keep the label-based model of KWOK and standalone modes, in the same simulator.
Turn it on with SIM_EMULATE=true and SIM_CLUSTER_SPEC; every variable is under Simulator emulate mode.
Node trees For each spec node the simulator keeps a tree under SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/<node>/, rendered from a hardware profile (simulator/pkg/hwemu/profiles/):
sys/: the powercap, cpufreq, hwmon and PCI attributes as the kernel nests them. An agent pod mounts it as its /host-sys. cpuinfo: mounted as the pod’s /proc/cpuinfo. One block per logical CPU with the profile’s model and topology, and a flags line with the flags its facts imply: hwp, and hwp_epp under intel_pstate, where cpufreq.hwp is true, and hypervisor on a virtual machine. A profile with none of them has no flags line; a corpus machine keeps its captured cpuinfo verbatim. state/: what the fake GPU tools read and write, such as NVML limits and energy, and the node’s energy ledger. bin/: nvidia-smi, rocm-smi and amd-smi, links to fakesmi, which the simulator installs in SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/lib/. The agent pod puts bin/ first on its PATH. One tick loop steps every node to wall time each SIM_EMULATE_TICK (default 1 s), on SIM_EMULATE_WORKERS workers: it reads back the limits the agent wrote, advances power, energy and frequency, and publishes an immutable snapshot. Requests read the latest snapshot and never step a node, so reading /telemetry/<node> any number of times changes nothing. With plain files, a value the hardware would refuse, out of range or unparsable, lands in the file and is reverted at the next tick, where a real driver would have failed the write; in FUSE mode the write fails at once. Either way it is reported as an event.
FUSE mode With SIM_HWEMU_FUSE=true (chart value emulate.fuse) the simulator serves each node’s sys/ and state/ through FUSE at SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/fuse/<node>/, and the emulated agents mount those (agent.emulated.fuse); cpuinfo, bin/ and dev/nvidiactl stay on the tree. The tree on disk becomes the simulator’s own copy, kept up to date for a restart to resume from. The simulated cluster runs this mode unless SIMCLUSTER_HWEMU=files.
A read is computed when it is made. The node steps to the time of the read, on the same substep grid a tick uses, so an energy counter moves between two reads within a tick, at 1 ms resolution, never goes back, and at a tick’s time reads what the tick computes. A value a reader saw is on disk before the read returns, so a restart never resumes below it. A write is answered when it is made. A value the driver refuses fails with the kernel’s errno (ENODATA for a locked RAPL limit, EINVAL, EBUSY, …) and changes nothing; any other value is in effect, and reads back normalized, before the write returns. Each write call is one store, as on sysfs, and every one is an event of the next tick. Files look as sysfs shows them. An attribute is 4096 bytes whatever its content, opening a file without write permission for writing fails with EACCES even for root, a write to a writable file the emulator does not model (such as intel_pstate/status) is taken and changes nothing, and nothing can be created, removed or renamed. A load change takes effect from the node’s last read when a read stepped the node past the previous tick, where plain files take it from the previous tick. It needs Linux and /dev/fuse. As root, as the chart runs it, the simulator mounts the file system in its own /tmp and bind-mounts each view at fuse/<node>/sys and fuse/<node>/state: that takes CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and the views reach the agents only with the root on a shared mount, propagation Bidirectional into the simulator and HostToContainer into each agent. The bind mounts are never unmounted: a restarted simulator binds its views over them, which reaches the running agents through that propagation, so they need no restart, and their reads fail with ENOTCONN until it does. Removing them takes umount -l on the host, or the end of the host’s mount namespace (make simcluster-down for the simulated cluster). As another user one FUSE mount at fuse/, through fusermount3, serves the same paths and is unmounted when the simulator stops; the unit tests run that way.
Plain files need none of this. They stay the default of the simulator, of the hwemu tests and of any host without FUSE; how they differ from a real node is under Deviations from a real cluster.
/control/<node> answers 409 for an emulated node: its limits are written to its files.
Governors and clocks A tree also holds the CPU and GPU governor files of its profile, so the agent’s governor discovery and control run against them. File classes: R is rendered and read-only, S is written by the emulator, A is writable by the agent, where a value the kernel would refuse is reported as a rejected event with its errno (joulie.sim.write.rejected, see Simulator Metrics): put back at the next tick with plain files, refused at the write in FUSE mode.
Files, under sys/ or state/ Class Where What the emulator does devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policyN/scaling_governor, scaling_min_freq, scaling_max_freq A every profile with cpufreq runs the governor as the kernel’s does, see governor and clock physics policyN/energy_performance_preference, energy_performance_available_preferences A, R (S on amd-pstate-epp) intel_pstate and intel_cpufreq with hwp, amd-pstate-epp refuses a non-zero EPP under performance on intel_pstate and amd-pstate-epp with EBUSY policyN/scaling_setspeed A profiles offering userspace the frequency userspace holds, within the policy’s limits; refused under any other governor devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/{schedutil,ondemand,conservative}/<tunable> A profiles offering those governors rate_limit_us, up_threshold, sampling_rate, freq_step, down_threshold, checked as the kernel checks them devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost, policyN/boost A, A acpi-cpufreq boost above the top table entry, from that entry only. Every policyN/boost reads the profile’s cpufreq.policyBoost at boot (default 0) while cpufreq/boost reads 1 and the CPUs boost, as on the nodes captured; a policy write equal to what its file shows changes nothing, one is refused with EINVAL while the global boost is off, and a global write of a new state sets every policy devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/{status,no_turbo,max_perf_pct,min_perf_pct,hwp_dynamic_boost} R, A, A, A, A intel_pstate, intel_cpufreq no_turbo lowers each policy’s maximum to the top non-turbo frequency devices/system/cpu/amd_pstate/status, policyN/boost R, A amd-pstate-epp boost per policy devices/system/cpu/intel_uncore_frequency/uncoreNN/ A, R, S intel-xeon6-2s-tpmi, intel-xeon-2s-multidie limits stored and checked; current_freq_khz follows the package load bus/pci/devices/<bdf>/power_dpm_force_performance_level A AMD GPUs takes the levels the profile accepts; a refused level goes back with the profile’s errno <bdf>/pp_dpm_{sclk,mclk,fclk,socclk,pcie} S AMD GPUs the DPM tables, with * on the level each domain runs at <bdf>/pp_od_clk_voltage A MI300X overdrive edits s 0, s 1, m 1 and c, only under manual or perf_determinism <bdf>/pp_power_profile_mode, <bdf>/pm_policy/{soc_pstate,xgmi_plpd} A W7900, MI300X stored and shown as the driver shows them nvml/gpuN/{clocks_sm_mhz,clocks_mem_mhz,pstate,clocks_event_reasons} S NVIDIA GPUs clocks, performance state and event reasons after each tick nvml/gpuN/{clocks_max_sm_mhz,clocks_max_mem_mhz,supported_clocks} R NVIDIA GPUs from the profile’s gpus.clocks nvml/gpuN/{locked_gpu_clocks,locked_mem_clocks} A NVIDIA GPUs written by nvidia-smi -lgc and -lmc; no query prints them, as NVML has no getter for a lock The fake tools act on the same files:
Command Effect rocm-smi --showperflevel, --setperflevel LEVEL, --showprofile, --setprofile N read or write the level; --setprofile switches to manual first amd-smi set -g GPU --perf-level LEVEL, --clk-limit sclk max MHZ; amd-smi metric --perf-level set or read the level, or the overdrive ceiling under manual; set --profile prints Not Yet Implemented nvidia-smi -i ID -lgc MIN,MAX, -rgc, -lmc MIN,MAX, -rmc set or clear a lock, one line per GPU then All done.; on a GPU without the lock, such as -lmc on Hopper, which has no run-time memory lock, it prints ... is not supported for GPU <bus id>. and Treating as warning and moving on., writes nothing there and exits 0, or exits 3 with --error-on-warning (-eow) nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.sm,clocks.mem,clocks.max.sm,clocks.max.mem,pstate,clocks_event_reasons.active (or clocks_throttle_reasons.active, the same file); nvidia-smi -q -d SUPPORTED_CLOCKS read the clock files nvidia-smi -ac, -rac refused as deprecated, non-zero exit nvidia-smi -pm 0, 1, DISABLED, ENABLED persistence mode off or on nvidia-smi --query-gpu=... --format=csv the header names each field by its canonical name, whichever alias was asked for (clocks.sm is clocks.current.sm, clocks_throttle_reasons.active is clocks_event_reasons.active) any option nvidia-smi does not have Invalid combination of input arguments. Please run 'nvidia-smi -h' for help. on stdout, exit 255 HWEMU_UNPRIVILEGED=1 in the tool’s environment runs it as a user without root: rocm-smi --setperflevel prints nothing, exits 0 and changes nothing on a profile with unprivilegedSetIsNoop, amd-smi set fails with Command requires elevation, and the nvidia-smi lock commands fail with Insufficient Permissions and exit 4.
Load from the workload can include peer transfers between the GPUs of a node (hwemu.Load.PeerTransfers): they share each receiver’s gpus.transfer.peerLinkGBps, and the bytes each GPU received and sent are counted in State (PeerRxBytes, PeerTxBytes).
Builtin hardware profiles Each profile in simulator/pkg/hwemu/profiles/ names the source of every value: a published document, a kernel or tool source line, a measurement described by its hardware only, or an assumption. A GPU profile extends a CPU host profile and keeps its CPU block.
Profile Hardware Control surface intel-xeon-2s-rapl 2x Xeon Platinum 8260 intel_pstate; RAPL PL1 and PL2; DRAM zones that refuse writes intel-xeon-6530-2s-rapl 2x Xeon Gold 6530 intel_cpufreq (intel_pstate passive); RAPL PL1 and PL2 intel-xeon-2s-psys 2x Xeon Gold 6530 intel_pstate; RAPL PL1 and PL2, plus a psys zone between the packages intel-xeon-2s-multidie 2x Xeon Platinum 9282, two dies per package one RAPL zone per die intel-xeon6-2s-no-powercap 2x Xeon 6787P intel_pstate only, no powercap intel-xeon6-2s-tpmi 2x Xeon 6787P TPMI RAPL with PL1, PL2 and PL4 amd-epyc-2s-energy-only 2x EPYC 9654 acpi-cpufreq; RAPL energy counters, no limits amd-epyc-9534-2s-energy-only 2x EPYC 9534 as above amd-epyc-2s-hsmp 2x EPYC 9655 amd-pstate-epp; HSMP socket caps in hwmon nvidia-h100-nvl-8gpu 8x H100 NVL on the 8260 host nvidia-smi, 200 to 400 W per GPU nvidia-h100-sxm-8gpu 8x H100 SXM on the 8260 host nvidia-smi, 200 to 700 W per GPU nvidia-h100-sxm-4gpu 4x H100 SXM5 on the 6530 host nvidia-smi, 200 to 700 W per GPU nvidia-l40s-4gpu 4x L40S on the 9534 host nvidia-smi, 100 to 350 W per GPU amd-instinct-mi300x-8gpu 8x Instinct MI300X on the 9654 host amdgpu hwmon, rocm-smi and amd-smi, 0 to 750 W per GPU; accelerator class, NFD pci-1200_1002 amd-radeon-pro-w7900-4gpu 4x Radeon PRO W7900 on the 9534 host amdgpu hwmon, rocm-smi and amd-smi; display class, NFD pci-0300_1002; the cap is pinned at 241 W per GPU intel-flex-170-4gpu 4x Data Center GPU Flex 170 on the 6530 host i915 hwmon, no tool, up to 150 W per GPU (power1_max, power1_rated_max), with a floor the hardware clamps to that sysfs does not show; display class, NFD pci-0380_8086 and Intel’s NFD rule labels vm-no-powercap KVM guest none: no powercap, no cpufreq The governor each profile ships with and the presets it can express (CPU performance, balanced, efficiency; GPU auto, sustained, efficient, low, peak, as pkg/governor maps them):
Profile CPU driver, shipped governor CPU presets GPU mechanism, presets amd-epyc-2s-energy-only, amd-epyc-9534-2s-energy-only acpi-cpufreq, schedutil all three (schedutil, conservative), global boost none amd-epyc-2s-hsmp amd-pstate-epp, performance all three through EPP, boost per policy none intel-xeon-2s-rapl, intel-xeon-2s-psys, intel-xeon-2s-multidie, intel-xeon6-2s-no-powercap, intel-xeon6-2s-tpmi intel_pstate with HWP, powersave all three through EPP, no_turbo none intel-xeon-6530-2s-rapl intel_cpufreq, schedutil all three (schedutil, conservative), no_turbo none amd-radeon-pro-w7900-4gpu as the 9534 as the 9534 amdgpu sysfs: auto, sustained (high), low, peak amd-instinct-mi300x-8gpu as the 9654 as the 9654 amdgpu sysfs: auto, efficient nvidia-h100-nvl-8gpu, nvidia-h100-sxm-8gpu as the 8260 as the 8260 nvidia-smi: every preset, sustained equivalent to auto nvidia-h100-sxm-4gpu as the 6530 as the 6530 as the H100 above nvidia-l40s-4gpu as the 9534 as the 9534 nvidia-smi: every preset, sustained locks the memory clock at its maximum intel-flex-170-4gpu as the 6530 as the 6530 none vm-no-powercap no cpufreq none none No builtin profile turns the receiver gate on.
Profile facts that shape what the agent reads:
physics.cpu.model: analytic, the power formula of idlePkgW and maxPkgW, or catalog-curve, the measured curve of the CPU’s catalog entry split over the packages. The 2x EPYC 9654 profiles (amd-epyc-2s-energy-only and amd-instinct-mi300x-8gpu, which extends it) run the curve of SPECpower_ssj2008 result 01203; the 9534 and HSMP profiles are analytic. limitBits of a powercap zone: the width of its power limit field, in raw power units. A limit past it wraps in the register, as on hardware. Unset, it is the MSR interface’s: 15 bits for PL1 and PL2, 17 on psys, 13 for PL4; intel-xeon6-2s-tpmi sets 18, the TPMI field. gpus.clocks.supported.smMaxByMem: memory clocks under which the GPU offers only the lower graphics clocks, each with the highest one. nvidia-smi -q -d SUPPORTED_CLOCKS lists the graphics clocks of such a memory clock up to that ceiling, and a memory clock lock holds the graphics clock at or below the ceiling of its memory clock, in the GPU’s power and speed and in clocks.sm (nvidia-l40s-4gpu). gpus.fieldSupport: an nvidia-smi query field and the token the tool prints in its place, such as power.min_limit: "[N/A]". The emulator never writes a value into that field’s file. nvidia-smi -pl on a GPU whose limit or range holds a token prints Changing power management limit is not supported for GPU: <bus id>. and Treating as warning and moving on., writes nothing, sets the other GPUs it was given and exits 0 after All done.; with --error-on-warning (-eow) it writes nothing and exits 3. No builtin profile sets it. base_frequency is rendered on the Intel profiles with HWP, so the agent’s cpu.landmarks.nominalFreqMHz is set. cpuinfo_max_freq follows turbo: it shows the top non-turbo frequency while intel_pstate/no_turbo or the amd-pstate boost turns turbo off. The W7900’s cap is pinned as measured: hwmon and both tools report minimum, maximum, default and current at 241 W, so the driver refuses every other value written to power1_cap (a joulie.sim.write.rejected event with error.type einval), rocm-smi --setpoweroverdrive prints the bound it violates and exits 0, and amd-smi set -o ppt0 prints “Power cap must be between 241W and 241W”. AMD publishes 295 W for the board; that is total board power, while 241 W is the package power limit the driver enforces and reports.
The Flex 170’s power1_max (class A) takes any value, as i915 does: a value in whole watts is kept, one between the hardware’s bounds is enforced, and one outside them reads back, after the next tick, as the bound the hardware clamps it to, 40 W at the bottom and 150 W at the top, so the agent’s readback reports it as an error. Writing 0 turns the limit off. The 40 W floor is assumed: sysfs does not show it, and Intel publishes none. gpus.intel.driver: xe renders the xe layout instead, with the limit on the package channel, power2_max.
The cluster spec apiVersion: sim.joulie.io/v1alpha1 kind: ClusterSpec metadata: {name: smoke} spec: defaults: kwok: true # KWOK annotation and taint on every node (the default) labels: {joulie.io/managed: "true"} baseLoad: {cpuUtil: 1.0, gpuUtil: 1.0, memoryIntensity: 0.2, cpuClass: cpu.compute_bound, gpuClass: gpu.compute_bound} facility: {ambientC: 20, amplitudeC: 5, periodH: 24, coolingZones: [{name: zone-a, offsetC: 0}, {name: zone-b, offsetC: 3}]} pools: - {name: intel, profile: intel-xeon-2s-rapl, count: 1, rack: rack-1, coolingZone: zone-a} - {name: sxm-nopm, profile: nvidia-h100-sxm-8gpu, count: 1, rack: rack-2, coolingZone: zone-b, overrides: {gpus: {persistenceMode: disabled}}} - {name: vm, profile: vm-no-powercap, count: 1} Each pool expands to count nodes named <pool>-<i> (or prefix and startIndex), with the profile’s labels, the defaults, then the pool’s labels, rack and cooling zone, plus sim.joulie.io/cluster and sim.joulie.io/pool. The annotation sim.joulie.io/profile names the profile. baseLoad is the utilization every emulated node runs at while no workload drives it; a pool’s baseLoad overrides the defaults field by field. The clusterspec command validates a spec and renders its Nodes:
go run ./simulator/cmd/clusterspec validate -spec tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml go run ./simulator/cmd/clusterspec render-nodes -spec tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml | kubectl apply -f - clusterspec validate|render-nodes|list -spec <file> [-profiles-dir <dir>]: -profiles-dir adds the local profiles of a directory to the builtin ones, and defaults to SIM_PROFILES_DIR. The simcluster command of the simulated cluster takes the same flag with the same default.
The simulator checks that each spec node exists in the cluster and names the same profile, and emits joulie.sim.node.mismatch once per change when it does not.
An NVIDIA profile can run with persistence mode off (overrides.gpus.persistenceMode: disabled): an idle GPU then drops the limit the agent wrote back to its default, as a GPU does when the driver unloads with no client, and the simulator records joulie.sim.cap.reset.
Restarts and recovery An existing tree is resumed, not rendered again: energy counters, the limits agents wrote and NVML state continue from disk, and the tree is completed from the layout, every missing entry created and nothing present touched, so a restart never replaces a file an agent pod holds open. Leftover state/.tmp/ensure-* directories are removed. Exported energy counters never decrease: they continue from a ledger in each node’s state/, so a restart shows in Prometheus as a gap in the rate, never as a counter reset. The ledger is rewritten each tick, in place and whole (padded with spaces) up to 2 KB, by rename above, so it holds the last whole tick also when the simulator is killed during a write. No energy accrues while the simulator is down.
A tree rendered for another profile, node or profile values, or one with an entry of the wrong kind (a file where a directory belongs, or a locked limit that is a directory, as an older simulator rendered it), stops the start with an error that names the node. To recover, make sure no agent pod mounts that node, remove SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/<node>, and start the simulator again: the node is rendered fresh, with its counters back at zero.
Telemetry The simulator pushes OpenTelemetry metrics (OTLP JSON over HTTP) for every node and for the facility, named after the hardware semantic conventions: hw.host.energy for the whole host, hw.energy per CPU package, DRAM zone and GPU. Only readings a real collector could measure are exported: a virtual machine node exports none. A Prometheus started with --web.enable-otlp-receiver takes the push directly, with no collector in between (see Prometheus settings). Events go to events.jsonl and, when a logs endpoint is set, are pushed as OpenTelemetry log records.
Names, units and Prometheus spellings: Simulator Metrics. Variables, and where the export deviates from the OpenTelemetry exporter specification: Simulator telemetry export. For Joulie inputs that expect a real exporter, SIM_EXPORTERS also serves Kepler 0.7, Kepler 0.12, dcgm-exporter and ROCm device-metrics-exporter formats, computed from the same counters. Workload runs A workload runs on the v1 engine, one run at a time, started through the run API or from SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH at startup. Each group of trace jobs becomes one batch/v1 Job, scheduled by the real scheduler onto the spec’s KWOK Nodes.
Every tick, the engine hands each node the load of the jobs running on it (each job holds as many logical CPUs as it requests, and its GPUs), so the node’s emulated power follows the work. Each job advances at the throughput the node’s limits leave it. The node’s energy delta is attributed per class: performance, standard, and idle for the unrequested share of the packages’ idle power. While a run is active the spec’s baseLoad does not apply. A finished pod is annotated sim.joulie.io/complete: "true", and a KWOK Stage moves it to Succeeded. A job that cannot progress, such as a gang that never runs whole, is reported as stalled, never completed by force. The run’s events and metrics go to <SIM_RUNS_DIR>/<runId>/otlp/ as OTLP JSON Lines. Workload Simulator compares the two engines; Workload Scenarios drive runs on the simulated cluster and evaluate them.
Tick cost A tick is mostly system calls on the nodes’ files. The readback does one lstat per agent-writable file and reads only the files written since its last read, and the emulator rewrites only the files whose content changed. In FUSE mode the tick reads back no file, since every write reached the node through its view, and the reads of the views step the nodes between ticks, a cost the agents’ reads pay instead. SIM_EMULATE_WORKERS defaults to GOMAXPROCS, at most 12, because those calls contend past about 12 workers.
The median tick of the benchmark below on a shared machine, approximate and machine-dependent:
Nodes Median tick 16 intel-xeon-2s-rapl about 11 to 13 ms 200 intel-xeon-2s-rapl about 105 to 115 ms 16 amd-epyc-2s-energy-only about 50 to 80 ms So 200 Intel nodes fit in the default 1 s tick without tmpfs. A start on an existing root compares the live tree with the layout and creates only the missing entries: resuming 200 Intel nodes takes about 0.7 s, rendering them on a fresh root about 12 s.
To measure on your machine (the trees go to TMPDIR; p50-ms is the median tick, the -live cases are the tick of FUSE mode, and a run as root matches the simulator’s container, since a non-root run pays two chmod calls per write of a file it may not write):
go test ./simulator/pkg/emulate/ -run '^$' -bench EM01Tick -benchtime 10x In a running simulator, joulie_sim_emulate_tick_duration_seconds and joulie_sim_emulate_tick_overruns_total (Simulator Metrics) show the cost.
