body:
Complete reference for all Joulie environment variables. These are set via Helm values or directly in the Deployment/DaemonSet manifests.
Defaults listed below are the code defaults. The Helm chart (charts/joulie/values.yaml) overrides some of them: notably, the controller manager NODE_SELECTOR defaults to joulie.io/managed=true in the chart even though the code default is node-role.kubernetes.io/worker.
Booleans. The agent, the controller manager and the simulator read every on/off variable the same way: true, 1, yes or on, and false, 0, no or off, in any case, with surrounding spaces ignored. Unset or empty means the default. Any other value keeps the default and logs one warning naming the variable, so a typo never flips a switch. The exceptions are SIM_OTEL_FILE_METRICS, OTEL_SDK_DISABLED and fakesmi’s HWEMU_UNPRIVILEGED, whose rows say how they are read.
Images The chart values agent.image.tag, controllerManager.image.tag and schedulerExtender.image.tag (and image.tag in the simulator chart) default to empty, which pulls the chart’s appVersion. A chart installed from oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie carries the version it was released with, so it runs the images of that release. A chart installed from a checkout has appVersion: latest and runs the newest stable release. Set a tag only to run other images, for example your own build.
Pre-releases (a GitHub pre-release, or a version such as 0.2.0-rc0) are published under their version only and never move latest.
Every image (joulie-agent, joulie-controller-manager, joulie-scheduler, joulie-simulator) is a multi-arch index of linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, so each node pulls the image of its own architecture. The kubectl plugin is released for linux and darwin, each on amd64 and arm64.
Agent Variable Default Description AGENT_MODE daemonset daemonset (one agent per node) or pool (shared agents with sharding) NODE_NAME (required in daemonset mode) Name of the node this agent manages RECONCILE_INTERVAL 20s How often the agent reconciles desired state METRICS_ADDR :8080 Address for the Prometheus metrics endpoint SPEC_READ_TIMEOUT 5m How long the agent tolerates failed reads of its NodeTwin spec, leaving the node as it is. Past it the agent relaxes every cap and puts the governor baseline back, as when the spec is gone, until a read succeeds. A Go duration such as 90s; a value it cannot parse keeps 5m SIMULATE_ONLY false If true, agent discovers hardware but does not apply power caps or governors (governor result disabled) HARDWARE_CATALOG_PATH (empty: the catalog embedded in the binary) Path to a hardware inventory catalog YAML that replaces the embedded one KUBE_CLIENT_QPS 50 Queries per second the agent’s Kubernetes client may send KUBE_CLIENT_BURST 100 Burst above KUBE_CLIENT_QPS the agent’s Kubernetes client may send Agent pool mode Variable Default Description POOL_NODE_SELECTOR joulie.io/managed=true Label selector for nodes managed by pool agents POOL_SHARDS 1 Total number of shards for pool mode partitioning POOL_SHARD_ID (from pod ordinal) Shard ID for this agent instance Agent DVFS control Variable Default Description DVFS_EMA_ALPHA 0.3 Exponential moving average smoothing factor for power tracking DVFS_HIGH_MARGIN_W 10.0 Power above cap (watts) to trigger frequency reduction DVFS_LOW_MARGIN_W 15.0 Power below cap (watts) to trigger frequency increase DVFS_STEP_PCT 10 Frequency throttle step size (%) DVFS_COOLDOWN 20s Minimum duration between DVFS adjustments DVFS_TRIP_COUNT 2 Consecutive samples outside margin before acting DVFS_MIN_FREQ_KHZ 1500000 Floor frequency for DVFS throttling (kHz) Agent governor control The agent always discovers the CPU and GPU governors of its node and publishes them in NodeHardware (see Governor discovery). It writes the presets of its NodeTwin, spec.cpu.governor and spec.gpu.governor, only with GOVERNOR_WRITES true; the controller manager writes those fields only with its own GOVERNOR_CONTROL on (see Governor control). The baseline it puts back lives in NodeHardware: it follows every discovery until the agent’s first governor write, so a change an operator makes before writes are on is what a restore puts back, and from that write it stays fixed until a restore. The agent puts it back when a field disappears.
Variable Default Chart Description GOVERNOR_WRITES false false Write the governor presets. false reports disabled for a preset and writes no preset. With false the agent still puts back the settings it changed in an earlier run (result restored), once, and writes nothing else. GOVERNOR_RESTORE_ON_EXIT true true On SIGTERM or SIGINT, put the baseline back before the agent exits, for every component it changed. A rolling update of the agent therefore restores the baseline and the new agent applies the preset again. SIGKILL and OOM kills restore nothing. Writes use the agent’s existing /host-sys mount, root user and privileges, the ones the DVFS fallback uses; the pod spec does not change. Without them the result is refused and NodeHardware shows writable: false. NVIDIA presets run nvidia-smi -i <pci bus id> -lgc or -lmc, so they need nvidia-smi in the agent (see “Agent GPU tools”); without it the result is error, as for caps. In the HTTP control mode (TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL or TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL http) and in pool mode the agent writes no governor and reports unsupported. What each preset becomes on each CPU driver and GPU family is in CPU support and GPU support. The results, their retries and the restore rules are in Governor control. Check them with: kubectl get nodetwins -o custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,CPU-GOV:.status.controlStatus.cpuGovernor.result,CPU-NATIVE:.status.controlStatus.cpuGovernor.applied,GPU-GOV:.status.controlStatus.gpuGovernor.result,GPU-NATIVE:.status.controlStatus.gpuGovernor.applied Agent telemetry and control backends Variable Default Description TELEMETRY_CPU_SOURCE host CPU telemetry source: host (the node’s RAPL files), http (TELEMETRY_CPU_HTTP_ENDPOINT), none TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL host CPU control backend: host, http, none TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL host GPU control backend: host, http, none TELEMETRY_CPU_HTTP_ENDPOINT (empty) HTTP endpoint for CPU telemetry, {node} replaced with the node name (e.g., http://sim:18080/otlp/telemetry/{node}). Each answer is one OTLP JSON ExportMetricsServiceRequest: the agent sums the hw.type=cpu components, from the rate of hw.energy or else the hw.power gauge, of the resource whose k8s.node.name is the node (a resource without it is read too). See HTTP input format. The legacy packagePowerWatts JSON is still read, with one warning per endpoint and node, until v0.4.0: its power is the first positive of packagePowerWatts and cpu.packagePowerWatts, and there is no reading when neither is positive. An answer over 8 MiB is an error. TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL_HTTP_ENDPOINT (empty) HTTP endpoint for CPU control (e.g., http://sim:18080/control/{node}) TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL_MODE (empty) CPU control mode override TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL_HTTP_ENDPOINT (empty) HTTP endpoint for GPU control (e.g., http://sim:18080/control/{node}) TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL_MODE (empty) GPU control mode override TELEMETRY_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 2 HTTP client timeout for telemetry/control requests, in whole seconds Agent chart values Helm values of charts/joulie that shape the agent pods. The DaemonSet and the emulated agents share one pod spec (joulie.agentPodSpec in templates/_helpers.tpl), so agent.tolerations, agent.runtimeClassName and the agent.extra* hooks apply to both; the pool StatefulSet takes none of them. Emulated agents ignore agent.hostNetwork and agent.privileged.
Value Default Effect agent.mode daemonset daemonset: one agent per node matching agent.daemonset.nodeSelector. pool: the StatefulSet joulie-agent-pool (see “Agent pool mode”). emulated: one Deployment per agent.emulated.nodes entry, for the simulated cluster. none: no agent. agent.tolerations - operator: Exists (every taint) Tolerations of the agent pods. The default tolerates every taint, so the agent runs on every node agent.daemonset.nodeSelector picks, GPU nodes with their vendor’s taint and dedicated pools included: the node selector, not the taints, decides where it runs. A list replaces the default, and [] tolerates none. A managed node the agent does not reach is still planned, its caps are never enforced, and its NodeTwin says so (see Managed nodes without an agent). agent.runtimeClassName "" RuntimeClass of the agent pods, for example the one of the NVIDIA container runtime, which puts the node’s driver tools into the container. agent.extraEnv [] EnvVar entries added after the chart’s own. agent.extraVolumes [] Volume entries added after the chart’s own. agent.extraVolumeMounts [] VolumeMount entries added to the agent container after the chart’s own. agent.emulated.root /var/lib/joulie-hwemu The simulator’s SIM_HWEMU_ROOT. Each emulated agent mounts its node’s tree from there: sys at /host-sys, cpuinfo over /proc/cpuinfo (read-only), state at /emu/state, bin at /emu/bin (read-only), <root>/lib at /emu/lib (read-only), and dev/nvidiactl at /dev/nvidiactl for an entry with devNvidiactl. agent.emulated.hostNodeSelector joulie.io/hwemu-host: "true" Node selector of the emulated agents: the node that holds the trees and runs the simulator. agent.emulated.path /emu/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin PATH of the emulated agents, so the emulated GPU tools come first. agent.emulated.fuse false Mount sys and state from the simulator’s FUSE views, <root>/fuse/<name>/sys and <root>/fuse/<name>/state, with mount propagation HostToContainer, for a simulator with emulate.fuse; the other mounts stay on the tree. The DaemonSet ignores it. agent.emulated.nodes [] One entry per emulated node, as simcluster agents writes them: name (the Node, also the literal NODE_NAME), profile, devNvidiactl, extraVolumes, extraVolumeMounts. Entry i becomes the Deployment joulie-agent-emu-<i>, with strategy Recreate, no host network and no privileges. A name that is not a Node name, or is listed twice, fails the render. Emulated agents are what the simulated cluster runs: one per node the DaemonSet would reach, judged from the DaemonSet’s own render.
Agent GPU tools The agent reads and caps NVIDIA GPUs by running nvidia-smi from its PATH. AMD GPUs need no tool: the agent reads and writes the power1_cap files of their amdgpu hwmon devices under /host-sys (see Agent host backends), which needs a root agent and a writable /host-sys, as the chart gives by default. It runs rocm-smi --showproductname only as a vendor probe, and never runs amd-smi. Intel GPUs need no tool either: the agent reads and writes the power1_max or power2_max files of their i915 or xe hwmon devices under /host-sys, with the same root agent and writable /host-sys, and reports the GPU control backend host-intel. The agent image (gcr.io/distroless/static) ships no GPU tool, and has no C library and no ELF loader, so mounting the host’s nvidia-smi alone is not enough: it is dynamically linked (file $(command -v nvidia-smi) on a GPU node shows it) and also needs the loader and the NVML library (libnvidia-ml.so.1). The hooks above are where these come in: agent.runtimeClassName for a container runtime that injects the driver’s tools and libraries, such as the NVIDIA one, or agent.extraVolumes and agent.extraVolumeMounts for a host directory, with agent.extraEnv.
The NVIDIA inventory is nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,power.min_limit,power.max_limit,power.limit,power.draw,name,power.default_limit --format=csv,noheader,nounits; a wrapper that answers for nvidia-smi must answer that query. NodeHardware gpu.capRangePerGpu.defaultWatts is its power.default_limit, and maxWatts when it prints none within the range; on AMD it is always maxWatts, because the driver rewrites power1_cap_default with the cap in force. gpu.powerDomains is the number of GPUs that hold a power limit of their own, published only when it is below gpu.count, as on two-die AMD packages such as the MI250X; the controller manager and the extender multiply the per-GPU maximum by it, and by the count when it is absent.
Which combination works on a real NVIDIA node is an open question: no recipe has been verified yet. After installing, check the GPU control status of every GPU node:
kubectl get nodetwins -o custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,GPU:.status.controlStatus.gpu.result,MESSAGE:.status.controlStatus.gpu.message A tool that cannot run shows as error with a message starting gpu inventory failed, or as blocked with no supported GPU backend detected when the vendor cannot be told either; the GPUs then keep their limits. On an AMD node without the amdgpu driver the message is gpu inventory failed: no amdgpu hwmon device under bus/pci/devices, and a cap the driver refuses, or a read-only /host-sys, is error naming the GPU’s bus id. On an Intel node labelled as one without an i915 or xe hwmon device it is gpu inventory failed: no i915 or xe hwmon device with a power limit under bus/pci/devices; Intel GPUs whose driver shows no power<N>_rated_max end blocked with the power limit range of the Intel GPUs is unknown, and a limit the hardware clamps is error with the value it reads back. The simulated cluster reproduces both sides: fakesmi fails as the real tool does when something it needs is missing (HWEMU_ROOTFS under Simulator hardware emulation), and the harness either mounts those files (toolDelivery: mounted) or not (toolDelivery: none).
Managed nodes without an agent The controller manager plans every managed node, whether or not an agent runs there, and says in the node’s NodeTwin whether one does: the condition AgentReporting in status.conditions, shown in the Agent column of kubectl get nodetwins. It is True (reason NodeHardwareCurrent) while an agent publishes the node’s NodeHardware, and False when no agent has published it (NoNodeHardware) or its last write is more than 15 minutes old (NodeHardwareStale): the caps in spec are then planned and not enforced. The controller manager logs a warning each time a node turns False, and counts the managed nodes per status and reason in the gauge joulie_twin_nodes_agent_reporting (Twin agent coverage). The usual causes are a taint the agent does not tolerate (agent.tolerations), a node outside agent.daemonset.nodeSelector, or an image without the node’s platform.
kubectl get nodetwins -o custom-columns='NODE:.spec.nodeName,AGENT:.status.conditions[?(@.type=="AgentReporting")].status,REASON:.status.conditions[?(@.type=="AgentReporting")].reason' Controller manager Variable Default Description RECONCILE_INTERVAL 1m How often the controller manager reconciles cluster state METRICS_ADDR :8081 Address for the Prometheus metrics endpoint LEADER_ELECT false Run the reconcile loop only on the leader of a coordination.k8s.io lease. Required before running more than one controller manager replica. Helm: controllerManager.leaderElection.enabled, which also creates the lease Role. POD_NAMESPACE joulie-system Namespace of the leader election lease. The chart sets it from the downward API. HARDWARE_CATALOG_PATH (empty: the catalog embedded in the binary) Path to a hardware inventory catalog YAML that replaces the embedded one NODE_SELECTOR node-role.kubernetes.io/worker Label selector for managed nodes RESERVED_LABEL_KEY joulie.io/reserved Label key for nodes excluded from policy decisions POWER_PROFILE_LABEL joulie.io/power-profile Node label key for the active power profile KUBE_CLIENT_QPS 50 Queries per second the controller manager’s Kubernetes client may send KUBE_CLIENT_BURST 100 Burst above KUBE_CLIENT_QPS the controller manager’s Kubernetes client may send Measured node power The controller manager writes each node’s measured power to NodeTwin.status.powerMeasurement.measuredNodePowerW. With NODE_POWER_SOURCE=prometheus, which the chart sets, it runs one grouped PromQL query per reconcile (GET <address>/api/v1/query) and reads every node from the answer; with http it reads one OTLP JSON document per node. The default preset otel reads the OpenTelemetry hardware metrics that producers push to Prometheus’ OTLP receiver: the rate of hw.energy, or the hw.power gauge, of the cpu and gpu components, keyed by the resource attribute k8s.node.name. Input metrics (OpenTelemetry) has the contract, every preset query and the Prometheus settings it needs.
The Chart column is what charts/joulie/values.yaml sets; “unset” means the code default applies.
Variable Default Chart Description PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS (empty) http://prometheus-operated.monitoring:9090 Prometheus the measured inputs are read from. The default of NODE_POWER_PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS and FACILITY_PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS. PROMETHEUS_NAME_TRANSLATION UnderscoreEscapingWithSuffixes unset Prometheus’ otlp.translation_strategy, which the controller manager must match: UnderscoreEscapingWithSuffixes, NoUTF8EscapingWithSuffixes, UnderscoreEscapingWithoutSuffixes or NoTranslation, case-insensitive. It spells the metric and label names of the otel presets, and under every facility preset the key labels of the zone, rack and node inputs, which are translated the same way. PROMETHEUS_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES auto unset Where the otel node power preset finds k8s.node.name. labels: on every series, which needs k8s.node.name in Prometheus’ otlp.promote_resource_attributes. target_info: joined from target_info on job and instance, which needs no promotion. auto: the labels form first, then the target_info form when the first returns nothing or a series lacks the node label; it keeps the form that works until that form returns nothing or fails, and logs every switch. PROMETHEUS_RATE_WINDOW 5m 5m Window of every rate() the inputs run, and the longest interval the http source measures an energy rate over. At least 10s, a whole number of seconds, and at least four export intervals of the producer, or rate() reads low. NODE_POWER_SOURCE static prometheus static (0 W), prometheus or http. An unknown value means static, with a warning. NODE_POWER_PRESET (empty: otel, or custom when NODE_POWER_PROMETHEUS_QUERY is set) unset The format the Prometheus query reads: otel, kepler (Kepler 0.10 and later: the active and idle energy counters of the CPU package and die zones, which never wrap, plus the GPU energy counter), kepler-legacy (Kepler 0.7 to 0.9: package and GPU energy) or custom. Every preset query is under The queries. A preset other than custom together with NODE_POWER_PROMETHEUS_QUERY stops the controller manager at start, so a query is never silently ignored. NODE_POWER_SCOPE components components components: the CPU packages plus the GPUs, the boundary of the twin’s budget (CPU TDP plus GPU TDP). host: the whole host (hw.host.energy and hw.host.power, or Kepler 0.7 platform energy), which exceeds the budget under load. kepler with host stops the controller manager at start. NODE_POWER_NODE_LABEL per preset: the translated k8s.node.name (k8s_node_name by default) for otel and custom, node_name for kepler, exported_instance for kepler-legacy unset The label that names the node in the query result. NODE_POWER_PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS unset Prometheus of the node power query only. NODE_POWER_PROMETHEUS_QUERY (empty) unset Your own PromQL, in watts, for the custom preset. With {node} it runs once per node with the node name filled in, and every series it returns is summed (a warning names a node whose query returns more than one). Without {node} it is summed by NODE_POWER_NODE_LABEL. NODE_POWER_HTTP_ENDPOINT (empty) unset With NODE_POWER_SOURCE=http: a URL with {node}, answering one OTLP JSON ExportMetricsServiceRequest per node, such as the simulator’s /otlp/telemetry/{node}. It is read with the rules of the otel preset under NODE_POWER_SCOPE; see HTTP input format. The legacy packagePowerWatts JSON is still read with a warning until v0.4.0: its power is the first positive of packagePowerWatts and cpu.packagePowerWatts, whatever NODE_POWER_SCOPE says, and 0 W when neither is positive. An answer over 8 MiB is an error (source: http-error). Deprecated aliases, removed in the next minor release: OPERATOR_NODE_POWER_SOURCE, OPERATOR_NODE_POWER_HTTP_ENDPOINT, OPERATOR_NODE_POWER_PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS, OPERATOR_NODE_POWER_PROMETHEUS_QUERY. They are read only when the new name is unset, and the controller manager logs a warning naming the replacement.
A custom query must return instantaneous power in watts. Energy exporters publish cumulative joules counters, which grow without bound, so they have to be converted with rate(); the presets already do:
rate(kepler_node_platform_joules_total{exported_instance="{node}"}[5m]) NODE_POWER_PRESET=kepler-legacy with NODE_POWER_SCOPE=host reads the same series without a custom query. Passing a counter directly makes measuredNodePowerW climb forever, which drives power headroom negative and cooling stress to 100% on every node. The controller manager logs a warning when a reading exceeds twice the node’s TDP.
Upgrading from v0.2: see Upgrading.
Power cap configuration Variable Default Description PERFORMANCE_CAP_WATTS 5000 Absolute CPU power cap for performance nodes (watts). The CPU of a GPU node gets it whatever the node’s profile. ECO_CAP_WATTS 120 Absolute CPU power cap for eco CPU-only nodes (watts). A GPU node never gets it: capping the CPU of a GPU node slows the GPU data feed by more than it saves. CPU_PERFORMANCE_CAP_PCT_OF_MAX 100 CPU cap as percentage of max for performance nodes CPU_ECO_CAP_PCT_OF_MAX 60 CPU cap as percentage of max for eco nodes CPU_WRITE_ABSOLUTE_CAPS false If true, write absolute watts instead of percentage GPU_PERFORMANCE_CAP_PCT_OF_MAX 100 GPU cap as percentage of max for performance nodes GPU_ECO_CAP_PCT_OF_MAX 60 GPU cap as percentage of max for eco nodes GPU_WRITE_ABSOLUTE_CAPS false If true, write absolute GPU watts instead of percentage GPU_MODEL_CAPS_JSON {} JSON map of GPU model name to {"minCapWatts": N, "maxCapWatts": M} CPU_ECO_CAP_ON_UNCAPPABLE_GPU_NODES false If true, a GPU node whose NodeHardware reports GPUs without control (status.gpu.controlAvailable false: Intel GPUs without a default limit in sysfs, NVIDIA boards whose power limits read [N/A]) gets the CPU caps of its profile, as a CPU-only node does, instead of running uncapped in eco. Other GPU nodes get no eco CPU cap whatever this says. GPU_PRODUCT_LABEL_KEYS joulie.io/gpu.product,nvidia.com/gpu.product,amd.com/gpu.product-name,beta.amd.com/gpu.product-name,amd.com/gpu.product,gpu.intel.com/product,amd.com/gpu.family Comma-separated node label keys to read the GPU product name from, first match wins. The AMD node labeller names the board in amd.com/gpu.product-name (and beta.amd.com/gpu.product-name); amd.com/gpu.product is the older key. Intel’s NFD rules name a data center GPU in gpu.intel.com/product (for example Flex_170). The AMD family code in amd.com/gpu.family (for example GC_11_0_0) names no board, so it comes last. When its GPU inventory fails, or names no model, the agent reads these default labels, in this order; it does not read this variable. The GPU caps apply to every GPU node, per physical GPU: a node whose agent lists GPUs, whose labels state a GPU count (joulie.io/hw.gpu-count, nvidia.com/gpu.count except when the single MIG strategy exposes MIG devices, product suffixed -MIG-, or Intel’s gpu.intel.com/device.count), or that advertises whole GPUs, MIG devices, AMD partitions or shared replicas (Shared and partitioned GPUs). A product read through GPU_PRODUCT_LABEL_KEYS loses the suffixes GPU feature discovery appends (-MIG-<profile>, -MIG-INVALID, -SHARED), so GPU_MODEL_CAPS_JSON and GPU_GOVERNOR_MODEL_PRESETS_JSON are keyed by the product without them.
Policy configuration Variable Default Description POLICY_TYPE static_partition Policy algorithm: static_partition, queue_aware_v1, or rule_swap_v1 STATIC_HP_FRAC 0.50 Fraction of nodes allocated to performance in static_partition, split across hardware families in proportion to their size, at least one node per family QUEUE_HP_BASE_FRAC 0.60 Base fraction of performance nodes in queue_aware_v1. The resulting count is split across hardware families in proportion to their size, at least one node per family QUEUE_HP_MIN 1 Minimum performance nodes in queue_aware_v1 QUEUE_HP_MAX 1000000 Maximum performance nodes in queue_aware_v1 QUEUE_PERF_PER_HP_NODE 10 Running or pending performance pods per performance node in queue_aware_v1 The controller manager exports the split as joulie_policy_family_nodes{family} and joulie_policy_family_performance_nodes{family}, where family is gpu:<model> or cpu:<model>. See Metrics.
Governor control Off by default. With GOVERNOR_CONTROL on, the controller manager writes a vendor-neutral governor preset into each managed node’s NodeTwin (spec.cpu.governor, spec.gpu.governor), chosen by the profile the node runs at; the agent maps it to the node’s native settings. Nothing changes on a node until its agent also runs with GOVERNOR_WRITES true. Which node gets which preset: Governor policy.
Variable Default Description GOVERNOR_CONTROL off off, cpu (CPU governors only), gpu (GPU governors only) or all. CPU_GOVERNOR_PERFORMANCE_PRESET performance CPU preset of performance nodes: performance (highest frequency at any load), balanced (demand-driven, quick ramp) or efficiency (demand-driven with an energy bias). CPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_PRESET efficiency CPU preset of eco nodes. Provisional: in the simulator’s governor exploration it saved 0.5 % energy for a 22.2 % eco p95 slowdown, above the experiment’s 20 % limit. CPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_BOOST empty on or off: frequency boost (turbo) with the eco preset, on nodes whose agent found a boost control (status.cpu.governor.boost). Empty leaves boost alone. CPU_GOVERNOR_ON_GPU_NODES false Write the CPU governor on GPU nodes too. GPU_GOVERNOR_PERFORMANCE_PRESET empty GPU preset of performance nodes: auto, sustained, efficient, low, peak, or empty for none. GPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_PRESET efficient GPU preset of eco nodes; set it to an empty value to write none. GPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_CEILING_PCT_OF_MAX 80 Compute clock ceiling of the efficient preset, in percent of the GPU’s maximum compute clock, in (0, 100]. Written only with efficient; a value out of range gives 80. The default is provisional: in the simulator’s governor exploration 75 slowed eco work past the eco class’s 20 % p95 limit and 80 did not. GPU_GOVERNOR_MODEL_PRESETS_JSON {} Presets per GPU model: {"<model>": {"performance": "<preset>", "eco": "<preset>", "ecoCeilingPctOfMax": <pct>}}. Keyed like GPU_MODEL_CAPS_JSON, by the GPU product label value, and also matched against the GPU model the agent reports. A field left out keeps the default above, "" writes none for that model, and an invalid field is dropped with a warning. GPU_GOVERNOR_SUSTAINED_ONLY_MULTI_GPU false If true, a node whose GPU preset is sustained gets it only while a running pod on it requests 2 or more GPUs (units of any GPU resource: whole GPUs, MIG devices, partitions, shared replicas), and no GPU governor otherwise. GPU presets: auto is the vendor default. sustained holds the data-path clocks (memory, fabric) at their maximum and keeps idle gating, leaving the compute clock free to idle; a demand-driven governor sees only a GPU’s own kernels, so a GPU that receives a peer transfer can stay at low data-path clocks, and on families where those clocks bound the transfer, sustained removes that limit at some idle power. No default selects it: opt a model in through GPU_GOVERNOR_MODEL_PRESETS_JSON once a measurement on that model shows the gain. efficient puts the compute clock under the ceiling and leaves the data path dynamic. low and peak are for experiments; peak turns idle gating off on AMD GPUs. These defaults are provisional until measured. Hardware modeling says what each preset means, and Governor policy which node gets which.
The overview dashboard’s “Agent: Governors” row plots the presets in effect (joulie_agent_governor_state) and the writes per result (joulie_agent_governor_writes_total).
Facility metrics The facility poller reads six inputs from Prometheus, each with one grouped query per poll. The outdoor ambient temperature, IT power and cooling power are one value each; the twin uses the IT power for PSU stress and the ambient temperature for cooling stress, and the controller manager logs PUE as (IT power + cooling power) / IT power. The zone, rack and node inputs return one series per cooling zone, rack or node (see “Node topology” below). An input whose query fails or returns nothing is unknown until a later poll reads it, never the value of an earlier poll. Every query is counted in joulie_twin_input_queries_total{input,result}, and the three single values are exported as joulie_twin_facility_* (Metrics).
Variable Default Chart Description ENABLE_FACILITY_METRICS false false Poll the facility inputs. The first poll runs at start. FACILITY_PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS, or http://prometheus-operated.monitoring:9090 when that is unset unset Prometheus of the facility queries only. FACILITY_POLL_INTERVAL 30s 30s How often the inputs are polled. 0 or less stops the controller manager at start. FACILITY_PRESET otel otel otel: the facility, cooling zone, rack and host metrics of the input contract, all six inputs. legacy: the datacenter_ambient_temperature_celsius, datacenter_total_it_power_watts and datacenter_cooling_power_watts names, the three single inputs only; deprecated, removed in v0.4.0. custom: only the inputs whose query is set below. FACILITY_AMBIENT_TEMP_QUERY from the preset unset Outdoor ambient temperature, one value in degrees Celsius. FACILITY_IT_POWER_QUERY from the preset unset Power of the IT equipment, one value in watts. FACILITY_COOLING_POWER_QUERY from the preset unset Power of the cooling, one value in watts. FACILITY_ZONE_AMBIENT_TEMP_QUERY from the preset unset Ambient temperature of each cooling zone, keyed by the translated joulie.cooling_zone.name label (joulie_cooling_zone_name by default), whose values are the nodes’ joulie.io/cooling-zone label values. FACILITY_RACK_POWER_QUERY from the preset unset Power of each rack in watts, keyed by the translated joulie.rack.name label (joulie_rack_name), whose values are the nodes’ joulie.io/rack label values. FACILITY_NODE_INLET_TEMP_QUERY from the preset unset Inlet temperature of each node, keyed by the translated k8s.node.name label (k8s_node_name). A query variable replaces its input’s query under any preset. A bare metric name is aggregated by the input’s key label, avg for a temperature and sum for a power, so FACILITY_IT_POWER_QUERY=ups_output_power_watts runs sum(ups_output_power_watts). Any other query is kept as written and must return one series, or for the zone, rack and node inputs one series per key carrying the key label.
Deprecated aliases, removed in v0.4.0: FACILITY_AMBIENT_TEMP_METRIC, FACILITY_IT_POWER_METRIC, FACILITY_COOLING_POWER_METRIC, the former names of the first three query variables. They are read only when the new name is unset, with a warning naming the replacement, and the bare metric name they hold keeps its meaning.
Node topology Joulie supports optional per-rack PSU stress and per-zone cooling stress. This is activated by adding standard node labels:
joulie.io/rack: physical rack identifier (e.g., rack-1) joulie.io/cooling-zone: cooling zone identifier (e.g., zone-a) When these labels are present, the controller manager computes PSU stress per rack instead of cluster-wide: the rack’s power is the facility’s rack power input (FACILITY_RACK_POWER_QUERY, keyed by the joulie.io/rack value) when it reads that rack, otherwise the sum of the estimated power of the rack’s nodes. The ambient temperature of a node’s twin is the most local one known: the node’s inlet temperature (FACILITY_NODE_INLET_TEMP_QUERY), then its cooling zone’s (FACILITY_ZONE_AMBIENT_TEMP_QUERY, keyed by the joulie.io/cooling-zone value), then the outdoor ambient. The twin model interfaces remain the same; topology just groups nodes for more accurate stress computation.
Nodes without topology labels fall back to cluster-wide stress computation, and still use their inlet temperature when the facility reads one.
Scheduler extender Variable Default Description EXTENDER_ADDR :9876 Bind address for the scheduler extender HTTP server METRICS_ADDR :9877 Address for the scheduler’s Prometheus metrics endpoint CACHE_TTL 30s Minimum interval between rebuilding the scoring maps from the informer cache, which watches NodeTwin and NodeHardware, so a score never reads the API server. TWIN_STALENESS_THRESHOLD 5m Duration after which NodeTwin data is considered stale With schedulerExtender.hostNetwork: true the chart deploys the extender with strategy Recreate: an old and a new pod cannot hold the host port on one node, so a rolling update would never finish. Pods are still scheduled while the extender restarts only if the scheduler configuration marks it ignorable: true; otherwise also set schedulerExtender.nodeName, so the new extender pod does not wait for the scheduler that waits for it.
Simulator This section covers the binaries under simulator/cmd. Each subsection names the binary that reads its variables. The simulator’s modes are described in Simulator.
Simulator basics The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) reads these in every mode.
Variable Default Description SIM_ADDR 127.0.0.1:18080; :18080 in a pod (where KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST is set) Listen address of the HTTP API. The API has no authentication: expose it only to trusted clients. The chart sets :18080. SIM_NODE_SELECTOR (empty: every Node) Label selector of the Nodes the simulator models. The chart sets joulie.io/managed=true. SIM_NODE_CLASS_CONFIG (empty) YAML file of label-matched node classes that override model parameters per node. SIM_HARDWARE_CATALOG_PATH (empty: the catalog embedded in the binary) A hardware catalog YAML that replaces the embedded one. SIM_K8S_POD_WATCH true List pods and nodes every SIM_POLL_INTERVAL. SIM_DEBUG_PERSIST_DIR /tmp/joulie-simulator-debug Directory of timeseries.csv, events.ndjson and snapshots of the debug endpoints (nodes.json, jobs.json, events.json, energy.json); empty disables them. SIM_FACILITY_AMBIENT_TEMP_C, SIM_FACILITY_TEMP_AMPLITUDE_C, SIM_FACILITY_TEMP_PERIOD_H 20, 5, 24 Outdoor ambient temperature of the facility model: a sine of this mean, amplitude and period in hours. In emulate mode the cluster spec’s facility block wins. SIM_STANDALONE false Run without Kubernetes (Standalone mode). Simulator thermal model The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) reads these variables at startup to build its base hardware profile. A node class in SIM_NODE_CLASS_CONFIG overrides one per node with the key in parentheses, under the class’s model:.
Temperature follows a first-order lag toward ambient plus power over the watts per degree, and is reported in the telemetry. Thermal throttling is off by default: both thresholds of a device are 0. Setting one variable of a pair turns it on, with the other at the value its row gives. In a node class set both thresholds, the full one above the start: a class with only a start threshold makes the simulator ignore every class, with one warning in the log, and a class with only a full threshold throttles from 0 °C. See Hardware Modeling, sections 5.5 and 6.6.
Variable Default Description SIM_CPU_AMBIENT_TEMP_C 24 CPU ambient temperature in °C (cpuAmbientTempC) SIM_CPU_THERMAL_TAU_MS 4000 CPU thermal time constant in milliseconds (cpuThermalTauMs) SIM_CPU_WATTS_PER_DELTA_C 8 CPU watts per °C above ambient at equilibrium (cpuWattsPerDeltaC) SIM_CPU_THERMAL_THROTTLE_START_C 0 (off) CPU temperature in °C where thermal throttling starts (cpuThermalThrottleStartC). 85 when only SIM_CPU_THERMAL_THROTTLE_FULL_C is set. SIM_CPU_THERMAL_THROTTLE_FULL_C 0 (off) CPU temperature in °C where thermal throttling reaches throughput 0 (cpuThermalThrottleFullC). 97 when only SIM_CPU_THERMAL_THROTTLE_START_C is set. SIM_GPU_AMBIENT_TEMP_C 24 GPU ambient temperature in °C (gpu.ambientTempC) SIM_GPU_THERMAL_TAU_MS 2500 GPU thermal time constant in milliseconds (gpu.thermalTauMs) SIM_GPU_WATTS_PER_DELTA_C 12 GPU watts per °C above ambient at equilibrium (gpu.wattsPerDeltaC) SIM_GPU_THERMAL_THROTTLE_START_C 0 (off) GPU temperature in °C where thermal throttling starts (gpu.thermalThrottleStartC). 82 when only SIM_GPU_THERMAL_THROTTLE_FULL_C is set. SIM_GPU_THERMAL_THROTTLE_FULL_C 0 (off) GPU temperature in °C where thermal throttling is full (gpu.thermalThrottleFullC). 92 when only SIM_GPU_THERMAL_THROTTLE_START_C is set. Simulator power limits The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) reads these variables at startup too. For a node whose labels match the hardware catalogue, a variable that is unset leaves the field to the catalogue; the built-in default applies only to hardware the catalogue does not know. A node class key (in parentheses) wins over both, and a value of 0 or less counts as unset. See Hardware Modeling, section 3.1.
Variable Default Description SIM_P_MAX_W sockets x catalogue TDP, else 420 Peak CPU power of the generic model, at full load and full frequency (pMaxW). A node with a measured curve uses the curve instead. SIM_CPU_SOCKET_CAP_MAX_W catalogue TDP, else 400 Upper end of the per-socket CPU cap: the node cap is split evenly over the sockets and clamped to this range (cpuSocketCapMaxW). SIM_CPU_SOCKET_CAP_MIN_W catalogue cTDP low end, else 0.55 x TDP, else 120 Lower end of the per-socket CPU cap (cpuSocketCapMinW). SIM_GPU_MAX_WATTS_PER_GPU catalogue maxBoardPowerW, else 300 Board power of one GPU at full load, and its highest cap (gpu.maxWattsPerGpu). SIM_GPU_MIN_CAP_WATTS_PER_GPU catalogue minBoardPowerW, else half the maximum, else 80 Lowest cap of one GPU (gpu.minCapWattsPerGpu). A catalogue minimum above a maximum set by a class or a variable is lowered to that maximum. A measured two-socket curve from the catalogue is scaled by sockets/2 on a node with another socket count.
Upgrading from v0.2: see Upgrading.
Simulator physics step The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) advances the model of a node outside the emulate-mode cluster spec only in a physics step, in simulated time; a read or a control never advances it. A step splits its time into equal substeps, and the energy it books is the integral of the instantaneous power over them. See Power Simulator.
Variable Default Description SIM_POLL_INTERVAL 15s (chart: 8s) Kubernetes mode: how often the simulator lists pods and nodes. A value of 0 or less logs a warning and takes 15s. SIM_PHYSICS_TICK 1s Kubernetes mode without emulate mode: every modelled node is stepped by the wall time since the last tick, in substeps of at most 100 ms. A value of 0 or less logs a warning and takes 1s. In emulate mode SIM_EMULATE_TICK steps them instead, and standalone mode steps them on its own tick. SIM_SA_SUBSTEP SIM_SA_DT Standalone mode: the longest physics substep, in simulated seconds. Each SIM_SA_DT tick is split into equal substeps no longer than this; the default is one substep per tick. A shorter substep follows the cap, frequency and thermal lags more closely at the cost of run time. Simulator hardware emulation fakesmi (simulator/cmd/fakesmi) stands in for nvidia-smi, rocm-smi and amd-smi on an emulated node. It runs as the tool its name says, through a bin/<tool> link, and reads and writes the node’s emulated hardware files instead of a driver. The agent does not read these variables; only fakesmi does.
Variable Default Description HWEMU_SYS_ROOT /host-sys The emulated node’s sys/ directory, where the amdgpu PCI and hwmon attributes live. The default is where an emulated agent pod mounts it. HWEMU_STATE_ROOT /emu/state The emulated node’s state/ directory: tools.json, which lists the tools the node has and the variant each one emulates, the NVML state of NVIDIA GPUs, and the per-card AMD values sysfs has no text attribute for (amdgpu/card<N>/). The default is where an emulated agent pod mounts it. HWEMU_ROOTFS / The file system the real tool would run in, where fakesmi looks for what the tool needs before it runs (below). The default is the agent container’s own root. HWEMU_UNPRIVILEGED false Run the tools as a user without root would: 1, true or another word Go’s strconv.ParseBool reads as true; anything else, unset included, means root. A set then changes nothing: nvidia-smi -pl, -pm, -lgc, -lmc, -rgc and -rmc exit 4 with Insufficient Permissions; amd-smi set and reset fail with PermissionError: Command requires elevation; a rocm-smi set exits 0 with the failure only at --loglevel debug, and prints nothing at all on a family whose profile sets gpus.dpm.unprivilegedSetIsNoop. Reads work as with root. A tool that tools.json does not list exits 127 with fakesmi: <tool> is not installed on this emulated node.
A listed tool first checks the requirements of its tools.json entry, in order, under HWEMU_ROOTFS: each requirement is a list of paths, and one existing path meets it. The first requirement with none of its paths present ends the call, before any GPU state is read, with the exit code and message the real tool gives without that file. The requirements are profile data (gpus.tools[].requires); a tool without requirements always runs. Every builtin GPU profile lists, the NVIDIA ones for nvidia-smi and the AMD ones for rocm-smi and amd-smi:
Tool Requirement (any one path) Exit Message nvidia-smi /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, the ELF loader 127 none: exec fails, which a shell reports as 127 nvidia-smi in this order, libpthread.so.0, libm.so.6, libdl.so.2, librt.so.1 and libc.so.6, each under /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, /lib64 or /usr/lib64 127 the loader’s nvidia-smi: error while loading shared libraries: <library>: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory for the first one missing nvidia-smi /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 or /usr/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1 12 NVIDIA-SMI couldn't find libnvidia-ml.so library in your system. ...; 12 is nvidia-smi’s “NVML Shared Library couldn’t be found or loaded” rocm-smi, amd-smi /usr/bin/env, from the scripts’ #!/usr/bin/env python3 127 none rocm-smi, amd-smi /usr/bin/python3 or /usr/local/bin/python3 127 /usr/bin/env: 'python3': No such file or directory In the simulated cluster, toolDelivery: mounted mounts one stub file at the first path of each requirement: seven on an NVIDIA node (the loader, the five libraries and NVML), two on an AMD node.
An empty HWEMU_ROOTFS is the default, /. Only a caller of package simulator/pkg/hwemu/smi that builds its own Env with an empty RootFS skips the checks, as the in-process agent tests do.
Simulator emulate mode In emulate mode the simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) emulates the bare-metal nodes a cluster spec lists: for each one it keeps a sysfs tree, /proc/cpuinfo and GPU tool state under SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/<node>/, and advances them on a fixed tick, so an unmodified agent pod that mounts them discovers and caps the node as it would a real one. Nodes the spec does not list keep the label-based model. /control/<node> answers 409 for an emulated node, whose limits are written to its files instead. See Emulate Mode.
Variable Default Description SIM_EMULATE false Turn emulate mode on. The simulator refuses to start when SIM_STANDALONE is also set, or when SIM_CLUSTER_SPEC is empty. Workloads run on the v1 engine; SIM_WORKLOAD_MODEL=legacy is refused, since a legacy trace cannot drive emulated nodes (see Simulator workloads and scenarios). SIM_CLUSTER_SPEC (empty) Path of the cluster spec, a sim.joulie.io/v1alpha1 ClusterSpec such as tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml. It names each node, its hardware profile, pool, rack and cooling zone, and the facility. SIM_HWEMU_ROOT /var/lib/joulie-hwemu Directory of the emulated trees: one <node>/ per spec node, lib/fakesmi and facility-ledger.json, and fuse/ with SIM_HWEMU_FUSE. One simulator holds it at a time; a second one fails to start. SIM_HWEMU_FUSE false Serve each spec node’s sys and state through FUSE at SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/fuse/<node>/, where the agents mount them: a write the kernel would refuse fails at once with its errno, a write it takes is in effect at once, and energy counters move at read time (FUSE mode). Needs /dev/fuse, and as root CAP_SYS_ADMIN; another user needs fusermount3. SIM_EMULATE_TICK 1s Physics tick: every spec node advances to wall time once per tick. A tick that runs late is counted and the next one catches up. The nodes outside the spec are stepped on the same tick (see “Simulator physics step”). SIM_GPU_RECEIVER_GATE profile Whether the receiver gate of peer transfers applies: profile follows each hardware profile’s gpus.transfer.receiverGate.enabled, off in every builtin profile; off disables it everywhere; on enables it on every GPU profile with the profile’s fractions, for what-if runs (a profile that leaves a fraction unset lets the whole link through). Any other value logs a warning naming the variable and takes profile. A gated copy slows the v1 job that makes it (see peer transfers). SIM_EMULATE_WORKERS 0 Nodes stepped in parallel; 0 means GOMAXPROCS, at most 12. A step is mostly system calls on the node’s files, which contend past about 12 workers (see Tick cost); a set value is used as given. SIM_FAKESMI_SOURCE /usr/local/lib/joulie/fakesmi The fakesmi binary to install as SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/lib/fakesmi, where every node’s bin/nvidia-smi, bin/rocm-smi and bin/amd-smi link points. It is replaced by rename, and only when its sha256 changed. The simulator image ships it at the default path. Empty skips the copy, for a run outside the image. KUBECONFIG client-go loading rules The cluster the simulator watches, so it can also run on a workstation. Without a kubeconfig it uses the in-cluster configuration. The simulator logs the API server it uses. Hardware profiles are the builtin ones in simulator/pkg/hwemu/profiles/, plus local ones from SIM_PROFILES_DIR. The facility values come from the spec’s facility block and fall back to SIM_FACILITY_AMBIENT_TEMP_C, SIM_FACILITY_TEMP_AMPLITUDE_C and SIM_FACILITY_TEMP_PERIOD_H.
A restarted simulator resumes the trees; a tree that no longer matches its spec node stops the start. Both, and the recovery, are under Restarts and recovery.

Simulator workloads and scenarios The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) drives a workload trace through the cluster. SIM_WORKLOAD_MODEL picks the engine: legacy outside emulate mode, v1 in emulate mode; the two are compared in Workload Simulator. The “Read by” column says which engine reads a variable.
Variable Read by v1 default Legacy default Description SIM_WORKLOAD_MODEL both v1 with SIM_EMULATE=true legacy otherwise legacy or v1. v1 without emulate mode and legacy with it stop the start. SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH both (empty) (empty) A trace file, or a directory of them, loaded at startup. Legacy replays it from startup. v1 starts it as an implicit run with id SIM_RUN_ID; a run that fails to start is logged and the run API stays open. The chart sets /etc/joulie-sim-trace/trace.jsonl outside emulate mode; in emulate mode set it through the chart’s extraEnv. SIM_WORKLOAD_TICK legacy 1s Period of the legacy workload loop. A value that does not parse as a duration, or of 0 or less, logs a warning and takes 1s. A v1 run advances once per emulator tick (SIM_EMULATE_TICK) and does not read it. SIM_WORKLOAD_IMAGE both registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9 the same Container image of every workload pod. SIM_BASE_SPEED_PER_CORE both 1 1 Work units one core, or one GPU, does per second at full speed. A v3 trace sizes work with it, so a job’s ideal runtime is its durationSec. A run request’s baseSpeedPerCore replaces it for that run. The default keeps workload pods off every Node outside the cluster spec, such as the one running the simulator. SIM_WORKLOAD_TOLERATIONS v1 kwok.x-k8s.io/node=fake:NoSchedule fixed, the same A JSON list of tolerations added to every pod; [] adds none. Nothing adds a GPU vendor’s toleration for a GPU request unless the cluster runs the ExtendedResourceToleration admission plugin. SIM_WORKLOAD_JOB_TTL v1 10m ttlSecondsAfterFinished of the Job objects; 0 deletes them as they finish. SIM_WORKLOAD_MAX_CREATES_PER_TICK both -1 (no cap) 20 Pods or Job objects created per tick; a positive count or -1. SIM_WORKLOAD_MAX_DELETES_PER_TICK legacy 10 Finished pods deleted per tick; a positive count or -1. SIM_WORKLOAD_KUBE_QPS, SIM_WORKLOAD_KUBE_BURST both 100, 200 30, 50 Rate limits of the workload’s Kubernetes client. SIM_WORKLOAD_STALL_REPORT v1 5m How long a running job must make no progress before joulie.sim.job.stalled, and the whole run before joulie.sim.run.stalled: a submitted job not done, no progress, no pod becoming Running or Succeeded, and every Pending pod Unschedulable, all for this long. Jobs not yet due never count. SIM_WORKLOAD_STALL_FORCE_COMPLETE legacy 120s How long a legacy job may make no progress before it is completed by force; -1 disables it. SIM_RUNS_DIR v1 $SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/_runs Directory of the run directories, <SIM_RUNS_DIR>/<run id>/: trace.jsonl, and otlp/simulator.metrics.jsonl and otlp/simulator.logs.jsonl. SIM_RUN_ID v1 run-<UTC yyyymmdd-hhmmss> Id of the implicit run of SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH; no slash, and not . or ... An invalid value stops the start with an error naming the variable, except SIM_WORKLOAD_TICK and SIM_BASE_SPEED_PER_CORE, which fall back to their defaults (see their rows). A variable only the other model reads logs a warning naming it; under v1 that includes SIM_WORKLOAD_TICK. A trace line may be up to 16 MiB. The legacy engine names pods sim-<jobId>, sanitized and at most 50 characters; a name already taken gets the lowest free -<n> suffix.
Run API. In v1 emulate mode the simulator serves one run at a time on its HTTP port; in every other mode these paths answer 412.
Path Method Answer /sim/v1/runs POST Starts a run. Body: runId, optional trace (a path inside SIM_RUNS_DIR, default <SIM_RUNS_DIR>/<runId>/trace.jsonl; any other path is refused, since the API has no authentication), optional clusterName, and options overriding the settings above for this run (owner, intent, completion, namespace, jobTTL, nodeSelector, tolerations, maxCreatesPerTick, stallReport, baseSpeedPerCore; an empty nodeSelector or tolerations clears the default, null keeps it). 201 with runId, jobs, groups and startedAt; 400 for a bad request or trace, naming the trace line; 409 while a run is active, or when the run id already has results. /sim/v1/runs/current GET 200 with the active or last run’s status: phase (running, finished or aborted), elapsedSeconds, allSubmitted, the jobs per state and runStalled; 404 before the first run. /sim/v1/runs/current/finish POST Ends the run; jobs not done end incomplete. ?cleanup=true also deletes the run’s Job objects, with their pods, or its bare pods, in the background: one deletecollection call per namespace by the run’s label, or one delete per object when the role lacks that verb. 200 with the final status once the run’s files are closed. Permissions. The joulie-simulator ClusterRole of charts/joulie-simulator grants get, list, watch, create and delete on pods and nodes, which both engines use. With rbac.workloadRuns (by default when emulate.enabled is true) it adds what a v1 run needs: patch and deletecollection on pods, for the completion annotation and the cleanup; get, list, watch, create, delete and deletecollection on batch jobs, for the Job objects and their cleanup; and get, list and watch on joulie.io nodetwins, which a run observes for each node’s schedulable class and never writes.
KWOK Stage. With SIM_WORKLOAD_COMPLETION=kwok, a pod ends only through a KWOK Stage named pod-complete that selects Running pods annotated sim.joulie.io/complete: "true": scripts/simcluster/manifests/stage-pod-complete.yaml, adapted from KWOK v0.8.0. It replaces KWOK’s own pod-complete Stage, which completes every Running pod a Job owns on a timer, before it did its work; the simulated cluster applies it after KWOK’s Stages. On another KWOK cluster, apply it the same way, or set SIM_WORKLOAD_COMPLETION=delete. simscenario run refuses a cluster whose pod-complete Stage does not select the annotation.
Scenario runner. scripts/simcluster/scenario.sh (make simcluster-scenario SCENARIO=<file>) has its own settings: Workload Scenarios. So do the other scripts of scripts/simcluster: Simulated Cluster.
Simulator telemetry export In emulate mode the simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) pushes OpenTelemetry metrics of every emulated node and of the facility as OTLP JSON over HTTP, for example straight to a Prometheus started with --web.enable-otlp-receiver. Events are always written to events.jsonl and pushed only when a logs endpoint is set. Names and Prometheus spellings: Simulator Metrics.
In every mode the simulator also answers reads of one node over HTTP: GET /otlp/telemetry/{node} and GET /telemetry/{node} serve the same OTLP JSON ExportMetricsServiceRequest, the format TELEMETRY_CPU_HTTP_ENDPOINT and NODE_POWER_HTTP_ENDPOINT read. ?format=legacy serves the deprecated packagePowerWatts JSON until v0.4.0, with one warning per process. ?format=otlp asks for the default explicitly; any other format value is refused with 400.
Variable Default Description SIM_EXPORTERS (empty) Comma-separated compatibility exporters to serve at /exporters/<name>/metrics: kepler-0.7, kepler-0.12, dcgm-4.8.4, amd-dme-1.5.2 (ROCm device-metrics-exporter v1.5.2, AMD GPUs). kepler-0.12 reads the RAPL zones of each node’s tree, and serves its GPU series only with SIM_KEPLER012_GPU. An unknown name stops the start and lists the valid ones. See Compatibility exporters. SIM_KEPLER012_GPU false true makes kepler-0.12 also serve kepler_node_gpu_* for NVIDIA GPUs, as Kepler’s experimental GPU option does. With the chart, set it in extraEnv. SIM_DCGM_HOSTNAME_LABEL hostname Host label of dcgm-4.8.4: hostname, or Hostname as dcgm-exporter releases up to 4.8.2 spell it. SIM_OTEL_FILE_DIR the value of SIM_DEBUG_PERSIST_DIR (default /tmp/joulie-simulator-debug) Directory of events.jsonl, one OTLP JSON LogsData object per line. Empty disables the files. SIM_OTEL_FILE_METRICS false Also append every metrics export to metrics.jsonl in the same directory, one MetricsData object per line. Read with Go’s strconv.ParseBool: 1, t, T, true, TRUE, True, or the same spellings of false; any other value stops the start. POD_NAME the host name Identifies this simulator instance in its own telemetry. The chart sets it from the downward API. OTEL_SDK_DISABLED false true, in any case, turns off both pushes, as the OpenTelemetry specification reads it; any other value leaves them on. OTEL_SERVICE_NAME joulie-simulator service.name of every resource. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (empty) Extra resource attributes, key=value pairs separated by commas. They never override service.instance.id, k8s.node.name or host.name. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT (empty) URL of the metrics push, used as is. For Prometheus: http://<prometheus>:9090/api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT (empty) URL of the events push, used as is. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (empty) Base URL for both signals: v1/metrics and v1/logs are appended. A per-signal variable wins. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_COMPRESSION, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL as the specification Headers (key=value,...), timeout in milliseconds, gzip or none, and the protocol, which must be http/json. Each has _METRICS_ and _LOGS_ variants that win for their signal. OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL 60000 Milliseconds between metrics pushes. A rate() window over the pushed counters should cover at least 4 intervals. OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER otlp none turns off that signal’s push. The export follows the OpenTelemetry exporter specification with three deviations:
Only http/json is supported; the specification’s default is http/protobuf, and any other protocol stops the start. Nothing is pushed without an endpoint; the specification’s default is http://localhost:4318. A 404 from the logs endpoint turns the logs push off after one warning. Prometheus has no logs receiver, so a base endpoint pointing at Prometheus would otherwise fail on every push. Points are cumulative: Prometheus rejects delta temporality unless its otlp-deltatocumulative feature is on. A push is retried on 429, 502, 503 and 504, honouring Retry-After, and never on 400 (such as out-of-order samples) or 500. Each request carries at most 64 node resources, plus the facility. A per-signal endpoint is used exactly as given, so it needs the full path; a base URL there is a common mistake.

Value Default Effect otel.metricsEndpoint "" OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT. otel.logsEndpoint "" OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT. otel.exportIntervalMillis 10000 OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL, in milliseconds since Helm cannot parse durations. otel.resourceAttributes {} OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, joined as key=value pairs. For queries, Prometheus should promote k8s.node.name and host.name onto the data series (otlp.promote_resource_attributes); without that, the node name is joined from target_info. See Prometheus settings.
Simulator hardware profiles The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) emulates a node from a hardware profile picked by name: one of the builtin profiles in simulator/pkg/hwemu/profiles/, or a local one. Local profiles stay outside the repository and are the only ones whose measured sources (measured: provenance) may name the machine they were measured on, such as a calibration of your own nodes. A builtin profile may cite a measurement too, but describes the machine by its hardware only.
Variable Default Description SIM_PROFILES_DIR (empty) Directory of local hardware profiles: every *.yaml file directly in it, each with a name equal to its file name without .yaml. Empty means the builtin profiles only, and so does a directory with no *.yaml in it, such as a mounted ConfigMap that holds no profile yet. Hidden entries (a leading dot) are skipped. A directory that does not exist, a path that is not a directory and a *.yml file, or a .yaml suffix in another case such as .YAML, are errors, never a fallback to the builtins. A local profile may extend (extends:) a builtin profile or another local one, by the same merge rules the builtins use. It may not take a builtin’s name, since one of the two would be hidden: give it a new name and extend the builtin instead. The simulator logs the local profiles once, as local profiles loaded dir=<dir> profiles=<names>.
kubectl plugin The kubectl joulie plugin reads the cluster through your kubeconfig, as kubectl does, and needs no configuration. It lists NodeTwin, NodeHardware, Node and Pod objects; without permission to list NodeHardware it shows no hardware and works otherwise. Install it with kubectl krew install joulie, or see the quickstart.
Command Shows kubectl joulie, kubectl joulie status the cluster summary (measured, capped and TDP power, nodes and their power per class, pods per class, average headroom, cooling and PSU stress, PUE) and one row per managed node kubectl joulie top the live dashboard: the status screen refreshed every --interval, with a power sparkline per node that takes one point per NodeTwin update; ↑ ↓ select, enter opens the node, p the pods, s sorts, r refreshes, q quits kubectl joulie node <node> one node: hardware, power, twin scores, the caps and governor presets planned and what its agent applied, its pods kubectl joulie pods every pod on a managed node: its class, its node and the node’s class; a performance pod on an eco node is flagged. A pod is performance when it asks for a performance node, as the controller manager reads it: the joulie.io/workload-class: performance annotation, or a node selector or node affinity on joulie.io/power-profile: performance; any other pod is standard kubectl joulie version the plugin version Flag Default Meaning -o, --output table json: the same data as one JSON document, for scripts -w, --watch off status and pods: open the live dashboard (-W is an alias) --interval 2s Refresh period of the live dashboard, at least 500ms --no-color off No colors. NO_COLOR=1 does the same, and output that is not a terminal has none -n, --namespace all namespaces pods only: list the pods of this namespace alone, which needs no permission to list pods cluster-wide. The node columns of the live dashboard then count these pods only --kubeconfig, --context, --cluster, --user, --server, --token as kubectl As in kubectl The node table of status and top:
Column Shows NODE The node name HARDWARE The node’s GPUs (count and model) or, on a node without GPUs, its CPUs (sockets and model), from its NodeHardware CLASS The NodeTwin’s schedulable class: performance, eco, draining or unknown POWER The measured node power, and a bar of it against the node’s capped power (its TDP while no cap is known); the power source when nothing measures it TREND The twin’s power trend in W/min; in top, a sparkline of the measured power, each block the share of the capped power it reaches CAP CPU·GPU The effective CPU and GPU caps in percent of the maximum; - for the GPU of a node without GPUs, and for both while the twin has no cap state HEADROOM, COOLING The twin’s predicted power headroom and cooling stress, 0 to 100 CPU, MEM Requested over allocatable, summed over the pods bound to the node that have not finished GPU GPUs requested over allocatable, counting whole GPUs, MIG devices, AMD partitions and shared replicas, each weighted by its share of a GPU; - for a node without GPU resources PODS The pods on the node; ▲n counts its performance pods AGENT The AgentReporting condition: ✓, ✗ with its reason, ? before the controller manager writes it The table drops the columns that do not fit the terminal, in this order: MEM, TREND, HARDWARE, COOLING, HEADROOM.
-o json prints time, summary (nodes per class, pods, performancePods, misplacedPods, podsError, measuredPowerW, cappedPowerW, tdpW, powerTrendWPerMin, avgHeadroomPct, avgCoolingStressPct, avgPsuStressPct, avgPUE, agentsReporting, agentsNotReporting), nodes for status and node (name, class, cpuModel, sockets, gpuModel, gpus, powerSource, measuredPowerW, cappedPowerW, tdpW, powerTrendWPerMin, cpuCapPct, gpuCapPct, headroomPct, coolingStressPct, psuStressPct, cpuRequestedPct, memoryRequestedPct, gpuRequestedPct, pods, performancePods, agentReporting, agentReason) and pods for pods and node (namespace, name, class, node, nodeClass, misplaced, cpu, gpus). cpuCapPct and gpuCapPct are left out while the twin has no cap state yet, and the GPU fields for a node without GPUs. podsError is set when the pods could not be listed; the pod counts are then unknown, not zero. A command’s list is present even when empty ("pods": []).
